docs.title: SyntropicOS Documentation
docs.text:
High-Performance Bare-Metal Application Framework & Cooperative OS

SyntropicOS is a zero-overhead, production-grade C99 framework designed for deeply embedded systems. It provides stackless multitasking, non-blocking drivers, industrial fieldbuses, and display graphics for targets ranging from 8-bit microcontrollers to 32-bit Cortex-M and RISC-V targets.

New here? Jump to the Getting Started Guide → for a 60-second no-hardware demo, a 3-minute tour of tasks, and setup instructions for Arduino, PlatformIO, CMake, Makefile, and vendor IDEs.

docs.title: Why SyntropicOS? (Design Rationale & Philosophy)
docs.text:
Deeply embedded systems present a fundamental architectural choice:

  1. Bare-Metal Super-Loops (while(1)): Simple to start and zero memory overhead. However, managing timers, state machines, protocol decoders, and non-blocking I/O in a single main loop quickly results in unmaintainable code. Any blocking call halts the entire microcontroller.
  2. Preemptive RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr): Multi-tasking where every task requires an allocated stack (512 B to 4 KB RAM per task). On microcontrollers with 2 KB to 16 KB total RAM, allocating thread stacks severely constrains memory. Preemptive switches also introduce race conditions, mutex contention, context-switch overhead, and potential stack overflows.
  3. The SyntropicOS Approach: A cooperative OS built around stackless coroutines (protothreads syn_pt). Tasks execute sequentially on a single system stack while syntax macros handle yielding and resumption. Continuation state costs 2 bytes of RAM per thread (uint16_t lc). Memory allocation is 100% static (zero malloc()), preventing runtime heap fragmentation.

SyntropicOS is not the first system to use stackless coroutines — Contiki OS (created by Adam Dunkels, who invented protothreads) popularized them for microcontrollers. The difference is that every SyntropicOS module is built from the ground up with the cooperative model in mind. Every driver, protocol stack, and subsystem exposes non-blocking _poll(), _update(), or _process() APIs that yield cooperatively. There are no blocking wrappers around third-party libraries or hidden busy-waits inside module code.

docs.title: Architecture & Framework Comparison
docs.text: Feature Bare-Metal Super-Loop Preemptive RTOS (FreeRTOS / Zephyr) SyntropicOS RAM per Thread 0 B 512 B – 4 KB per task (stack pointer) 2 B per thread (uint16_t lc) Concurrency Model Manual state machines in main loop Preemptive multi-threading Cooperative protothreads (syn_pt) Memory Allocation Static Dynamic heap or static pool allocation 100% Zero-Heap / Static Context Switch Cost Zero CPU register push/pop & stack frame swap Zero (C99 switch continuation jump) Race Conditions None (single thread execution) High (requires mutexes, semaphores, spinlocks) None across yield points Execution Safety Low (blocking functions freeze system) Stack overflow risk High (no thread stack overflow risk) Target Hardware 8-bit to 32-bit MCUs 32-bit MCUs (typically >32 KB RAM) 8-bit to 32-bit MCUs (2 KB+ RAM)

docs.title: 1. Stackless Protothreads (syn_pt)
docs.text: Protothreads provide sequential, non-blocking flow control inside standard C functions without requiring separate stacks. - Continuation & Explicit Yield Intent: PT_BEGIN() expands to a switch(pt->lc) jump table. Yield macros record __LINE__ in pt->lc and return explicit scheduling intent: PT_PASS() / PT_WAIT_UNTIL() return PT_IDLE (no immediate work left this round), while PT_CONTINUE() / PT_CONTINUE_IF_NEEDED() return PT_MORE (chunk finished, more work waiting). - RAM Footprint: Stores only a uint16_t continuation variable (2 bytes RAM). - Variable Lifetime: Local variables inside a protothread function do not persist across yields. Persistent state must be stored in static variables, global contexts, or a struct passed via user_data.

docs.title: 2. Cooperative Task Scheduler (syn_sched)
docs.text: The scheduler dispatches one eligible SYN_Task per syn_sched_run() call using ranked selection (Overdue -> Work -> Poll -> Round Reset) ordered by SYN_Prio (SYN_PRIO_CRITICAL = 0 .. SYN_PRIO_LOW = 3) and per-priority round-robin. - Bounded Starvation Windows: Configurable per-priority wait bounds (1 / 5 / 15 / 50 ms defaults via syn_sched_set_max_wait()) prevent active high-priority work from starving lower-priority tasks indefinitely. - Zero Dynamic Allocation: The application owns and allocates the SYN_Task array statically. - Tickless Idle & Native Blocking: Includes PT_BLOCK_* event blocking (SYN_TASK_BLOCKED) and low-power sleep (syn_sched_run_tickless(), or syn_sched_run_tickless_ex() when SYN_Timer deadlines must also wake the CPU) when no tasks are ready.

docs.title: 3. Ground-Up Non-Blocking Module Ecosystem
docs.text: Every driver and protocol module in SyntropicOS is written from scratch as a cooperative, non-blocking state machine. Modules expose _poll(), _update(), or _process() entry points (e.g. syn_modbus_poll(), syn_button_update(), syn_ble_gatt_process_att_pdu()) that do a bounded unit of work and return immediately. No module internally blocks, busy-waits, or calls delay().

docs.title: Technical Specifications At-a-Glance
docs.text: Feature Design Specification Concurrency Cooperative protothreads (syn_pt). Continuation state costs 2 bytes RAM per thread. Task Scheduler Cooperative task runner (syn_sched). Task descriptors (SYN_Task) cost 44 bytes RAM per task on 32-bit targets (80 bytes on 64-bit targets; standalone SYN_PT is 2 bytes). Memory Allocation 100% Zero-Heap / Static Allocation. No malloc() or dynamic pool fragmentation over long runtimes. Execution Model Every driver & protocol stack is written as a non-blocking state machine. Compatibility Standard C99. Compiles with GCC, Clang, IAR, Keil, STM32CubeIDE, and Arduino IDE.

docs.title: ⚡ Core, Utilities & Multitasking (Multitasking → · Core & Utilities →)
docs.text:
• Protothreads (syn_pt): Stackless coroutines for non-blocking task execution.
  • Task Scheduler (syn_sched): Cooperative task runner with ranked dispatch & starvation bounds.
  • Active Objects (syn_ao): FSM state machine + mailbox + task runner actor model.
  • Event Flags, Mutexes & Mailboxes: Priority-inheriting mutexes, 32-bit event flags, and SPSC mailboxes.
  • Core Utilities, Pools & Wire Codecs: Static pools/slabs, streams, Q16.16 linear algebra, JSON, CBOR, Protobuf, LZ4, and CRC.

docs.text:
• Buttons (syn_button): Debounced buttons, multi-click tap gestures, long-press, auto-repeat, and combos.
  • Rotary Encoder (syn_encoder): Quadrature rotary decoding and velocity tracking.
  • LED Controller (syn_led): Pattern blinking, flash sequences, and Morse sequences.
  • Software PWM (syn_soft_pwm): Timerless PWM generation on arbitrary GPIO pins.

docs.title: 📡 Communications & Protocol Stacks (Read Comm Docs →)
docs.text:
• Ethernet & IP Protocol Suite (syn_eth / syn_dhcp / syn_icmp / syn_autoip / syn_netcfg): Zero-heap Ethernet II, ARP, DHCP client, ICMP Echo ping, RFC 3927 AutoIP fallback, and Link Up/Down state machine.
  • COBS Framing (syn_cobs): Zero-overhead 0x00-delimited packet framing.
  • Packet Router (syn_router): Addressed packet dispatch (Master/Slave Node IDs) with ACKs.
  • Industrial Modbus (syn_modbus): Modbus RTU & Modbus TCP Master/Slave stacks.
  • Building Automation (syn_bacnet / syn_dali): BACnet MS/TP (ISO 16484-5) & DALI Lighting (IEC 62386) protocol engines.
  • M-Bus Metering (syn_mbus): EN 13757 European utility meter bus decoder.
  • Automotive ISO-TP & J1939: CAN bus multi-frame transport, UDS, CANopen, and heavy vehicle PGN/SPN decoders.
  • USB 2.0 Device & Host Core (syn_usb / syn_usb_host / syn_usb_cdc / syn_usb_hid): Zero-heap USB 2.0 device & host core engines, CDC ACM, HID, MIDI, and MSC class drivers.

docs.title: Arduino Compatibility Guide
docs.text:
Professional-grade multitasking and modular drivers for the Arduino ecosystem

SyntropicOS is designed to scale from high-performance bare-metal targets (STM32, RP2040) down to accessible environments like Arduino, providing a professional upgrade path for complex projects without leaving the Arduino IDE.

docs.title: Option A: Arduino Library Manager (Recommended)
docs.text:
SyntropicOS is listed in the official Arduino Library Manager. This is the easiest way to install and keep the library updated.

  1. In Arduino IDE: Tools → Manage Libraries... (or Ctrl+Shift+I)
  2. Search for SyntropicOS
  3. Click Install

No manual ZIP downloads or Git cloning required.

docs.title: Option B: Git Clone
docs.text:
If you need a specific development branch or want to contribute to the code:

  1. Open a terminal and run: 

    cd ~/Arduino/libraries
git clone https://github.com/outlookhazy/SyntropicOS.git

  2. To update later: cd ~/Arduino/libraries/SyntropicOS && git pull

docs.title: Option C: Download ZIP
docs.text:
1. Go to github.com/outlookhazy/SyntropicOS
  2. Click the green Code button → Download ZIP
  3. In Arduino IDE: Sketch → Include Library → Add .ZIP Library
  4. Select the downloaded ZIP file

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
After installing, open File → Examples → SyntropicOS. You should see:

  • Blink — LED blink using the cooperative scheduler
  • SerialCLI — Command-line interface over serial
  • SensorLogger — Dual-channel ADC sampling, EMA filtering, and statistics
  • MotorFSM — Finite state machine controlling a DC motor ramp
  • PID_TempControl — Closed-loop integer PID temperature controller with thermal plant simulation
  • Telemetry_CBOR — Zero-heap binary CBOR encoding, COBS packet framing, and CRC16 validation
  • SysMonitor — Multi-task software watchdog monitoring and circular error logging
  • MotionPlanner — Jerk-limited S-curve trajectory planning over a PubSub event bus
  • PicoBlink — Raspberry Pi Pico bring-up blink and diagnostics (RP2040 only)
  • PicoDualCore — Raspberry Pi Pico AMP dual-core mailbox & CLI demo (RP2040 only)

If you see these, you're ready to go.

docs.title: Example Architecture & Multi-Tab Sketches
docs.text:
Complex SyntropicOS examples (such as ButtonEvents and SensorLogger) use a clean Multi-Tab Structure:

  • Tab 1 (.ino Main Sketch): Focused purely on application logic, event callbacks, and hardware setup. Zero scheduler boilerplate clutter.
  • Tab 2 (sys_init.h / tasks.h): Encapsulates OS cooperative scheduling (syn_sched), background protothread task loops (PT_BEGIN / PT_END), and serial logger setup.

When you open an example from File → Examples → SyntropicOS, the Arduino IDE automatically loads both tabs. You can customize Tab 1 for your own application without needing to modify the underlying OS loop in Tab 2.

docs.title: Your First Sketch
docs.text:
Open File → Examples → SyntropicOS → Blink and upload it. The on-board LED will start blinking.

Here's what the code does, line by line:

#include <SyntropicOS.h>                 // SyntropicOS library
#include <syntropic/sched/syn_sched.h>  // Scheduler (runs your tasks)
#include <syntropic/output/syn_led.h>   // LED driver (blink patterns)

static SYN_Sched sched;    // The scheduler — manages all your tasks
static SYN_Task  tasks[1];  // Array of tasks (we have just one)
static SYN_LED   led;       // LED state — tracks the blink pattern

The task function — this is like a mini loop() that the scheduler calls repeatedly:

static SYN_PT_Status blink_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task)
{
    PT_BEGIN(pt);            // Required at the start of every task
    for (;;) {               // Loop forever (the scheduler handles timing)
        syn_led_update(&led); // Update the LED pattern
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 50);  // Wait 50ms, let other tasks run
    }
    PT_END(pt);              // Required at the end of every task
}

Setup and loop — familiar Arduino territory:

void setup()
{
    // Initialize the LED on the built-in pin, blinking 500ms on / 500ms off
    syn_led_init(&led, LED_BUILTIN, SYN_LED_ACTIVE_HIGH);
    syn_led_blink(&led, 500, 500);

    // Create the task and start the scheduler
    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "blink", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, NULL);
    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 1);
}

void loop()
{
    syn_sched_run(&sched);   // Run one ready task
}

docs.title: The Problem with delay()
docs.text:
In a normal Arduino sketch, delay(500) freezes everything for 500ms. Nothing else can run — no serial reading, no sensor polling, nothing.

// ❌ BAD: delay() blocks everything
void loop() {
    digitalWrite(LED_BUILTIN, HIGH);
    delay(500);                        // <-- Nothing else can happen for 500ms!
    digitalWrite(LED_BUILTIN, LOW);
    delay(500);
    int sensor = analogRead(A0);       // Only runs once per second
}

SyntropicOS solves this. Each task can pause itself without blocking the others.

docs.title: Tasks — Multiple loop() Functions
docs.text:
Think of a task as its own mini loop(). The scheduler calls each task in turn, and each task can pause at any point to let the others run.

Here's the basic pattern:

static SYN_PT_Status my_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task)
{
    PT_BEGIN(pt);             // Always start with this

    for (;;) {                // Your task's main loop
        // Do something...
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 500);   // Pause 500ms (others keep running!)
        // Do something else...
        PT_PASS(pt);                       // Let other tasks run this round
    }

    PT_END(pt);               // Always end with this
}

That's it. Three rules:

  1. Start with PT_BEGIN(pt);
  2. End with PT_END(pt);
  3. Pause cooperatively so other tasks can run:
  4. PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, ms) — wait at least ms milliseconds
  5. PT_PASS(pt) — no immediate work left right now; let other tasks run this round
  6. PT_CONTINUE(pt) — finished one chunk and more work is waiting; share CPU while staying active

docs.title: How It Works (Without the Jargon)
docs.text:
When your task hits PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 500), it bookmarks where it stopped and returns to the scheduler. The scheduler runs other tasks. After 500ms, the scheduler calls your task again, and it resumes from the bookmark — right where it left off.

You don't need to understand how the bookmarking works. Just follow the pattern.

docs.title: ⚠️ Two Rules to Remember
docs.text:
1. Use static for variables that need to survive across delays. Regular local variables are lost when a task pauses. Mark them static.

  2. Don't use switch statements inside a task body. Move them into a helper function, or use if/else if instead.

// ✅ Use 'static' for persistent variables
static int count = 0;
count++;
PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 1000);  // 'count' survives

// ✅ Move switch logic into a helper
static void handle_mode(int m) { switch(m) { /* ... */ } }
handle_mode(mode);  // Call from task body

For detailed explanations, examples, and advanced patterns, see the full Cooperative Multitasking documentation.

docs.title: Multiple Tasks
docs.text:
You can run as many tasks as you want:

static SYN_Task tasks[3];  // Room for 3 tasks

void setup() {
    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "blink",  blink_task,  SYN_PRIO_HIGH,     NULL);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "serial", serial_task, SYN_PRIO_CRITICAL, NULL);  // Higher priority (0 = highest)
    syn_task_create(&tasks[2], "sensor", sensor_task, SYN_PRIO_HIGH,     NULL);
    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 3);
}

All three run concurrently. No blocking. No threads. No heap allocation.

docs.title: Priority
docs.text: The second-to-last argument in syn_task_create() is the SYN_Prio priority level (SYN_PRIO_CRITICAL, SYN_PRIO_HIGH, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, SYN_PRIO_LOW). Lower enum values = higher priority (SYN_PRIO_CRITICAL = 0 is highest). Equal-priority tasks rotate round-robin, and each priority level enforces a default maximum wait window (1 ms, 5 ms, 15 ms, 50 ms) so active higher-priority tasks cannot starve lower-priority tasks indefinitely.

docs.title: CLI (Command Line Interface)
docs.text: SyntropicOS includes a serial command parser. See the SerialCLI example. Open the Serial Monitor at 115200 baud and type help to see available commands.

docs.title: LED Patterns
docs.text:
The LED driver supports more than just on/off:

syn_led_on(&led);                           // Solid on
syn_led_off(&led);                          // Off
syn_led_blink(&led, 200, 200);             // Fast blink
syn_led_flash(&led, 100, 100, 5);          // Flash 5 times, then stop
syn_led_pattern(&led, "... --- ... |", 150); // SOS in Morse code

docs.title: Filters and Sensors
docs.text: See the SensorLogger example for how to read analog pins with noise filtering and running statistics (min, max, mean, variance).

docs.title: State Machines (FSM)
docs.text: See the MotorFSM example for a table-driven state machine that transitions between states on commands and events.

docs.title: Disabling Unused Modules
docs.text:
By default, all SyntropicOS modules are available. Because Arduino cores compile with -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections and link with --gc-sections, unused functions in library .c files are stripped automatically by the linker.

Important (Arduino IDE Translation Units): Arduino IDE compiles library .c files in libraries/SyntropicOS/src/ separately without -I<sketch_dir>. A syn_config.h placed in your sketch folder applies only to headers compiled into your .ino translation unit (header-only utilities and inline definitions), not to separately compiled library .c files.

To apply SYN_USE_* or static-buffer sizing overrides across all library .c translation units, use one of these approaches:

  1. Library-level syn_config.h (Arduino IDE): Copy SyntropicOS/src/syntropic/syn_config_template.h to SyntropicOS/src/syn_config.h inside your libraries/SyntropicOS/ folder and set unused modules to 0: 
    #define SYN_USE_MQTT    0   // Disable MQTT
#define SYN_USE_FFT     0   // Disable FFT
#define SYN_USE_CAN     0   // Disable CAN bus
  2. Compiler flags (platformio.ini or platform.local.txt): Pass -I<config_dir> or -DSYN_USE_...=0 via build_flags in PlatformIO or compiler.c.extra_flags / compiler.cpp.extra_flags in Arduino's platform.local.txt.

docs.title: Supported Boards
docs.text:
SyntropicOS works on any board supported by the Arduino IDE:

Board Status Notes Arduino Uno / Nano / Mega ✅ 32 KB flash / 2 KB SRAM — linker strips unused code; use library-level syn_config.h or build flags to shrink static buffers ESP32 / ESP32-S3 ✅ Plenty of resources, everything enabled STM32 (STM32duino) ✅ Blue Pill, Nucleo, etc. RP2040 (Arduino-Pico) ✅ Raspberry Pi Pico SAMD21 / SAMD51 ✅ Adafruit Feather M0/M4, Arduino Zero Teensy 3.x / 4.x ✅ Full support

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"syn_assert_failed" undefined — Add this to your sketch: 

extern "C" void syn_assert_failed(const char *file, int line) {
    Serial.print("ASSERT: "); Serial.print(file);
    Serial.print(":"); Serial.println(line);
    for (;;);  // Halt
}

Sketch too large for Uno — Place syn_config.h in libraries/SyntropicOS/src/ (or pass -D flags via platform.local.txt / PlatformIO build_flags; see above) to disable unused modules and reduce static buffer sizes (SYN_LOG_BUF_SIZE, SYN_CLI_LINE_BUF_SIZE, SYN_UART_RX_BUF_SIZE).

Nothing happens after upload — Make sure your loop() calls syn_sched_run(&sched). Without it, no tasks will execute.

docs.title: Getting Started with SyntropicOS
docs.text:
SyntropicOS is a C99 cooperative multitasking operating system, driver layer, and protocol framework for microcontrollers. Tasks run on the main stack with zero heap allocation (malloc is never called) and 2 bytes of continuation state per protothread.

Choose where to start:

  • No hardware handy? Run a two-task demo on Linux or macOS in Section 1.
  • New to protothreads? Read Section 2: How Tasks Work (3-Minute Tour).
  • Setting up a board or IDE? Jump to Section 3: Add to Your Project and Section 4: First MCU Firmware.

docs.title: 1. Try It in 60 Seconds (No Hardware)
docs.text:
You can run the scheduler, timed delays (PT_TASK_DELAY_MS), event-flag blocking (PT_BLOCK_EVENT), and structured logging on Linux or macOS with any C99 compiler (gcc or clang).

From a SyntropicOS checkout, save this file as host_demo.c:

#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 199309L
#include <stdio.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "syntropic/syntropic.h"

/* ── Minimal host system port & console output ─────────────────────────── */
void syn_port_enter_critical(void) {}
void syn_port_exit_critical(void) {}

uint32_t syn_port_get_tick_ms(void) {
    struct timespec ts;
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (uint32_t)((uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000ULL + (uint64_t)ts.tv_nsec / 1000000ULL);
}

static void console_out(const char *str, size_t len) {
    (void)fwrite(str, 1, len, stdout);
    (void)fflush(stdout);
}

/* ── Application tasks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define EVT_PING (1UL << 0)
static SYN_EventFlags s_events;

static SYN_PT_Status producer_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    static uint32_t sent;
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (sent = 1; sent <= 3; sent++) {
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 200);          /* Pause 200 ms without blocking */
        SYN_LOG_I("PROD", "Ping #%lu", (unsigned long)sent);
        syn_event_flags_set(&s_events, EVT_PING); /* Wake consumer_task */
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

static SYN_PT_Status consumer_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    static uint32_t received = 0;
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    while (received < 3) {
        PT_BLOCK_EVENT(pt, task, &s_events, EVT_PING); /* Sleep until EVT_PING */
        received++;
        SYN_LOG_I("CONS", "Got ping #%lu", (unsigned long)received);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

int main(void) {
    static SYN_Task tasks[2];
    static SYN_Sched sched;

    syn_log_init(console_out, SYN_LOG_INFO);
    syn_event_flags_init(&s_events);

    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "producer", producer_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, NULL);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "consumer", consumer_task, SYN_PRIO_HIGH,   NULL);
    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 2);

    /* Returns false once both tasks reach PT_END(pt) */
    while (syn_sched_run(&sched)) {
        struct timespec nap = {0, 1000000L}; /* 1 ms idle sleep */
        nanosleep(&nap, NULL);
    }
    return 0;
}

Compile and run:

cc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Isrc host_demo.c \
  src/syntropic/sched/syn_sched.c \
  src/syntropic/sched/syn_mutex.c \
  src/syntropic/sched/syn_event_flags.c \
  src/syntropic/log/syn_log.c \
  src/syntropic/util/syn_fmt.c \
  src/syntropic/port_stubs/syn_port_stubs.c \
  -o host_demo && ./host_demo

Expected output:

[     200] I/PROD: Ping #1
[     201] I/CONS: Got ping #1
[     401] I/PROD: Ping #2
[     402] I/CONS: Got ping #2
[     602] I/PROD: Ping #3
[     603] I/CONS: Got ping #3

What happened:

  1. Both tasks ran sequentially on the single main stack — no OS threads and no malloc().
  2. PT_TASK_DELAY_MS paused producer_task for 200 ms while letting the rest of the program run.
  3. PT_BLOCK_EVENT parked consumer_task in SYN_TASK_BLOCKED (zero polling) until syn_event_flags_set() woke it.

docs.title: Anatomy of a Task
docs.text:
Think of each task as an independent for (;;) loop that pauses cooperatively instead of calling a blocking delay():

static SYN_PT_Status my_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);                        /* 1. Required at top of task body */

    for (;;) {
        do_some_nonblocking_work();
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 100); /* 2. Bookmark line & return to scheduler */
    }

    PT_END(pt);                          /* 3. Required at bottom of task body */
}

Preemptive RTOS threads allocate a separate 512 B–4 KB stack per task. A SyntropicOS protothread (SYN_PT) stores a 2-byte bookmark (uint16_t line number; 44 bytes total per scheduled SYN_Task on 32-bit MCUs). When a task hits a PT_* macro, it saves its line number and returns to syn_sched_run(). On its next turn, it jumps straight back to that bookmark.

docs.title: Which Pause Macro Should I Use?
docs.text: Goal Macro Behavior Wait ms milliseconds PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, ms) Pauses this task for at least ms; other tasks keep running. Sleep until signaled by ISR or task PT_BLOCK_EVENT(pt, task, &ev, mask) Parks task (SYN_TASK_BLOCKED, zero polling) until event bit is set. Related: PT_MUTEX_LOCK, PT_BLOCK_STREAM, PT_BLOCK_CONDITION. Wait until an expression is true PT_WAIT_UNTIL(pt, cond) Checks cond once per scheduler round until true. Yield for the rest of this round PT_PASS(pt) Reports no more work this round (PT_IDLE). Slice a long loop (DSP, crypto, I/O) PT_CONTINUE_IF_NEEDED(pt, task) Yields (PT_MORE) only when a peer task needs CPU time.

docs.title: Keeping State Across Pauses (The Two Rules)
docs.text:
Because a task returns from the C function on every pause, keep two rules in mind:

  1. Stack variables reset across pauses. Store values that must survive across a PT_* yield in a context struct passed via user_data (best when running multiple instances of a task) or in static variables (fine for single-instance tasks). Re-reading task->user_data above PT_BEGIN(pt) is safe because the function runs from the top before jumping to its bookmark.
  2. Do not place a C switch directly inside PT_BEGIN..PT_END. (PT_BEGIN expands to a switch jump table.) Use if / else if, or put switch statements inside a normal helper function.
typedef struct {
    SYN_GPIO_Pin pin;
    uint32_t period_ms;
    uint32_t toggles;
} BlinkCtx;

static void log_milestone(uint32_t count) {
    switch (count) { /* switch inside a helper function is always fine */
    case 10: SYN_LOG_I("LED", "10 toggles"); break;
    default: break;
    }
}

static SYN_PT_Status blink_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    BlinkCtx *ctx = (BlinkCtx *)task->user_data; /* Re-fetched on every wake */

    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        syn_gpio_toggle(ctx->pin);
        ctx->toggles++;                  /* Persists inside caller-owned BlinkCtx */
        log_milestone(ctx->toggles);
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, ctx->period_ms);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

With user_data, two independent tasks can share blink_task:

static BlinkCtx fast_led = { .pin = LED_A_PIN, .period_ms = 200,  .toggles = 0 };
static BlinkCtx slow_led = { .pin = LED_B_PIN, .period_ms = 1000, .toggles = 0 };

syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "led_fast", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, &fast_led);
syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "led_slow", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_LOW,    &slow_led);

docs.title: 3. Add to Your Project
docs.text:
Compiler Requirement: C99 or newer with __has_include support — GCC >= 5 (arm-none-eabi-gcc, riscv-none-embed-gcc, host gcc), Clang / ARM Compiler 6, IAR EWARM >= 8, or Arduino IDE.

Arduino IDEPlatformIOCMake (Submodule)Makefile (Submodule)STM32CubeIDE / Keil / IAR
  1. Open Tools → Manage Libraries... (Ctrl+Shift+I).
  2. Search for SyntropicOS and click Install.
  3. Open File → Examples → SyntropicOS → Blink and upload to your board.

See the Arduino Compatibility Guide for multi-tab sketch patterns and board notes.

Add SyntropicOS to platformio.ini:

[env:disco_f407vg]
platform = ststm32
board = disco_f407vg
framework = stm32cube
build_flags =
    -std=c99
    -Iinclude
lib_deps =
    https://github.com/outlookhazy/SyntropicOS.git

Add the submodule to your project:

git submodule add https://github.com/outlookhazy/SyntropicOS lib/SyntropicOS
git submodule update --init

In CMakeLists.txt:

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(my_firmware LANGUAGES C)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 99)

add_subdirectory(lib/SyntropicOS)

add_executable(my_firmware
    src/main.c
    # Pick the port matching your target from src/port/:
    lib/SyntropicOS/src/port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.c
)

# Optional: directory holding your syn_config.h (if you use one)
target_include_directories(my_firmware PRIVATE include)

# Define your MCU family when using port_stm32_hal.c outside CubeIDE/PlatformIO:
target_compile_definitions(my_firmware PRIVATE STM32F4xx)

# syntropic = portable headers & sources; syn_stubs = weak fallbacks for unused ports
target_link_libraries(my_firmware PRIVATE syntropic syn_stubs)

# Strip unused functions and data at link time
target_compile_options(my_firmware PRIVATE -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections)
target_link_options(my_firmware PRIVATE -Wl,--gc-sections)

sources.mk exports SYN_INC (lib/SyntropicOS/src), SYN_SRCS (all portable .c modules), and SYN_STUB_SRCS (syn_port_stubs.c):

SYN_DIR := lib/SyntropicOS
include $(SYN_DIR)/sources.mk

CFLAGS  += -std=c99 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -DSTM32F4xx -Iinclude -I$(SYN_INC)
LDFLAGS += -Wl,--gc-sections

SRCS += src/main.c
SRCS += $(SYN_SRCS)
SRCS += $(SYN_DIR)/src/port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.c
SRCS += $(SYN_STUB_SRCS)
  1. Add SyntropicOS/src (not the repo root) to your compiler include paths so #include "syntropic/syntropic.h" resolves.
  2. Enable C99 mode and dead-code stripping (-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections and -Wl,--gc-sections).
  3. Compile src/syntropic/**.c, your target port from src/port/<platform>/, and src/syntropic/port_stubs/syn_port_stubs.c.

See IDE Setup Guides for click-by-click screenshots/paths in STM32CubeIDE, VS Code + Cortex-Debug, Keil uVision, and IAR.

docs.title: Ready-Made Hardware Ports (src/port/)
docs.text:
Include the port file matching your target — no custom HAL code is needed for supported boards:

Target Platform Port Source Target Notes STM32 (Cube HAL) src/port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.c Supports F0/F1/F4/F7/G0/H7/L4/C0/U0. Include port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.h for SYN_PORT_STM32_PIN() and syn_port_stm32_register_uart(). STM32F4 (Bare-Metal) src/port/stm32f4/port_stm32f4.c Direct CMSIS register port (zero HAL dependency; includes startup_stm32f407.c & stm32f407.ld). Raspberry Pi RP2040 / RP2350 src/port/rp2040/port_rp2040.c Pico SDK (-DPICO_BOARD=...; add port_rp2040_multicore.c when SYN_USE_MULTICORE=1). ESP32 src/port/esp32/port_esp32.c ESP-IDF GPIO, UART, SPI, I2C, ADC, flash, and system tick port. WCH CH32V307 (RISC-V) src/port/ch32v307/port_ch32v307.c QingKe V4F bare-metal port (-DCH32V307=ON in CMake). Arduino src/port/arduino/port_arduino.cpp Cross-board Arduino C++ core (+ port_arduino_multicore.cpp on Arduino-Pico). POSIX Host Sockets src/port/posix/port_posix_socket.c Non-blocking TCP/UDP socket backend for Linux/macOS host testing.

For custom MCUs, see the Porting Guide — a minimal scheduler + GPIO bring-up only requires syn_port_system.h and syn_port_gpio.h.

What syn_stubs (syn_port_stubs.c) Does

Linking syn_port_stubs.c provides SYN_WEAK defaults for every syn_port_* function so your project links even if your port only implements GPIO and UART (skipping CAN, SPI, or Flash). Stubs are fail-fast traps, not silent no-ops: calling an unimplemented port function invokes syn_assert_failed(__FILE__, __LINE__).

docs.title: 4. First MCU Firmware (Blink and Serial Log)
docs.text:
Two cooperative tasks — one blinking an LED every 500 ms, one logging uptime every 2 seconds:

STM32 (Cube HAL)Raspberry Pi Pico (Pico SDK)Arduino / ESP32 / STM32duino 
#include "main.h" /* CubeMX-generated clocks, GPIO, and UART handles */
#include "syntropic/syntropic.h"
#include "port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.h"

extern UART_HandleTypeDef huart2;

/* Works with CubeMX labels (LD2_GPIO_Port, LD2_Pin) or raw (GPIOA, GPIO_PIN_5) */
#define LED_PIN SYN_PORT_STM32_PIN(GPIOA, GPIO_PIN_5)

static SYN_PT_Status blink_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        syn_gpio_toggle(LED_PIN);
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 500);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

static SYN_PT_Status log_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        SYN_LOG_I("APP", "Uptime: %lu ms", (unsigned long)syn_port_get_tick_ms());
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 2000);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

int main(void) {
    static SYN_Task tasks[2];
    static SYN_Sched sched;

    /* 1. Standard CubeMX clock + UART init (1 kHz SysTick feeds syn_port_get_tick_ms) */
    HAL_Init();
    SystemClock_Config();
    MX_USART2_UART_Init();

    /* 2. Bind huart2 to UART slot 0 for console logging, and configure LED pin */
    syn_port_stm32_register_uart(0, &huart2);
    syn_port_serial_init(115200);
    syn_log_init(SYN_LOG_INFO);
    syn_gpio_init(LED_PIN, SYN_GPIO_OUTPUT);

    /* 3. Register static tasks (SYN_PRIO_CRITICAL = 0 highest .. SYN_PRIO_LOW = 3) */
    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "blink", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, NULL);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "log",   log_task,   SYN_PRIO_LOW,    NULL);

    /* 4. Start cooperative scheduler */
    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 2);
    syn_sched_run_forever(&sched);
}

#include "pico/stdlib.h"
#include "syntropic/syntropic.h"

#define LED_PIN 25 /* On-board GP25 LED on Pico */

static SYN_PT_Status blink_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        syn_gpio_toggle(LED_PIN);
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 500);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

static SYN_PT_Status log_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        SYN_LOG_I("PICO", "Uptime: %lu ms", (unsigned long)syn_port_get_tick_ms());
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 2000);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

int main(void) {
    static SYN_Task tasks[2];
    static SYN_Sched sched;

    stdio_init_all(); /* Initializes USB CDC / UART stdio used by port_rp2040.c */
    syn_port_serial_init(115200);
    syn_log_init(SYN_LOG_INFO);
    syn_gpio_init(LED_PIN, SYN_GPIO_OUTPUT);

    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "blink", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, NULL);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "log",   log_task,   SYN_PRIO_LOW,    NULL);

    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 2);
    syn_sched_run_forever(&sched);
}

#include <SyntropicOS.h>

static SYN_Task tasks[2];
static SYN_Sched sched;

static SYN_PT_Status blink_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        syn_gpio_toggle(LED_BUILTIN);
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 500);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

static SYN_PT_Status log_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        SYN_LOG_I("APP", "Uptime: %lu ms", (unsigned long)syn_port_get_tick_ms());
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 2000);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

void setup() {
    syn_port_serial_init(115200);
    syn_log_init(SYN_LOG_INFO);
    syn_gpio_init(LED_BUILTIN, SYN_GPIO_OUTPUT);

    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "blink", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, NULL);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "log",   log_task,   SYN_PRIO_LOW,    NULL);
    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 2);
}

void loop() {
    syn_sched_run(&sched);
}

docs.title: 5. Optional Configuration (syn_config.h)
docs.text:
You do not need syn_config.h to get started. All 199 standard modules are enabled by default, and compiling with -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections plus -Wl,--gc-sections strips unused code automatically.

Create syn_config.h on your include path (auto-detected via #if __has_include("syn_config.h")) when you want to:

  1. Speed up builds or save static RAM by compiling out unused subsystems (#define SYN_USE_BLE 0, #define SYN_USE_TLS 0, etc.).
  2. Tune static buffer sizes (for example SYN_LOG_BUF_SIZE or SYN_UART_RX_BUF_SIZE on small-RAM MCUs).
  3. Enable any of the 9 opt-in hardware features (off by default because they require extra port hooks or dedicated RAM/Flash):
  4. SYN_USE_TICKLESS — Low-power tickless idle sleep (syn_sched_run_tickless*; requires syn_port_sleep_until())
  5. SYN_USE_MULTICORE — Dual-core AMP spinlocks & cross-core mailboxes (syn_port_spinlock.h)
  6. SYN_USE_DMA — Hardware DMA & cache coherency port (syn_port_dma.h)
  7. SYN_USE_I2C_ASYNC / SYN_USE_SPI_ASYNC — Interrupt/DMA non-blocking bus queues
  8. SYN_USE_CAN_FD — 64-byte CAN FD payloads in syn_can
  9. SYN_USE_PORT_AES — Hardware AES/GHASH offload (syn_port_aes.h)
  10. SYN_USE_COREDUMP — Crash core dump to flash (SYN_COREDUMP_FLASH_ADDR)
  11. SYN_USE_METRICS — Runtime counters, gauges, and histograms

Copy the documented template into your include folder:

cp lib/SyntropicOS/src/syntropic/syn_config_template.h include/syn_config.h
Common syn_config.h Tuning Parameters & Defaults Parameter Default Description SYN_SCHED_PRIO_LEVELS 4 Priority levels (SYN_PRIO_CRITICAL = 0 .. SYN_PRIO_LOW = 3, max 255) SYN_SCHED_MAX_WAIT_*_MS 1 / 5 / 15 / 50 Max starvation window per priority (CRITICAL / HIGH / NORMAL / LOW) SYN_MUTEX_MAX_WAITERS 4U Tracked contended waiters per SYN_Mutex for priority inheritance SYN_LOG_LEVEL SYN_LOG_DEBUG (1) Compile-time minimum log level (0 = TRACE .. 5 = FATAL, 6 = NONE) SYN_LOG_BUF_SIZE 192 Stack buffer size for syn_log() formatting (bytes) SYN_LOG_TIMESTAMP 1 Prefix log lines with [tick] millisecond timestamp SYN_LOG_COLOR 0 Emit ANSI color codes by severity SYN_CLI_LINE_BUF_SIZE 128 Maximum CLI command line length (bytes) SYN_CLI_HISTORY_DEPTH 0 CLI command history ring depth (0 = disabled) SYN_UART_TX_BUF_SIZE / RX_BUF_SIZE 128 Per-instance buffered SYN_UART ring sizes (bytes) SYN_UART_MAX_INSTANCES 2 Maximum simultaneous buffered SYN_UART instances SYN_CRC_USE_TABLE 1 1 = lookup-table CRC, 0 = compact bitwise CRC SYN_DISABLE_ASSERT (undefined) Define to strip runtime SYN_ASSERT() checks in release builds

See examples/PicoBlink/syn_config.h for a minimal bring-up configuration and src/syntropic/syn_config_template.h for all 208 switches.

docs.title: 6. First-Boot Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Firmware halts immediately in an infinite loop: A SYN_ASSERT() failed or your code called an unimplemented syn_port_* weak stub. Set a breakpoint on syn_assert_failed, or define a strong handler in main.c to print the offending file and line: 
    void syn_assert_failed(const char *file, int line) {
    /* Print over UART/SWO/RTT or inspect 'file' and 'line' in debugger */
    (void)file;
    (void)line;
    for (;;) {}
}
  • PT_TASK_DELAY_MS pauses forever: syn_port_get_tick_ms() is stuck at 0. Verify your 1 kHz timer interrupt is enabled (for example SysTick_Handler calling HAL_IncTick() on STM32).
  • No SYN_LOG_* output on STM32Cube HAL: Call syn_port_stm32_register_uart(0, &huartX) before syn_port_serial_init(), or pass a custom sink callback (syn_log_init(my_rtt_write, SYN_LOG_INFO)).
  • syn_config.h in an Arduino sketch folder has no effect on library .c files: Arduino IDE compiles libraries without -I<sketch_dir>. Place syn_config.h in libraries/SyntropicOS/src/ or use PlatformIO build_flags (see Arduino Guide).

docs.title: IDE Integration & Setup Guides
docs.text: Step-by-step setup guides for integrating SyntropicOS into standard microcontroller IDEs and toolchains: STM32CubeIDE, VS Code (PlatformIO & CMake), Keil MDK-ARM, IAR Embedded Workbench, and Arduino IDE.

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text:
1. Add SyntropicOS Source Tree:
  2. Copy or add a git submodule of SyntropicOS into your STM32CubeIDE project root folder (e.g. Middlewares/Third_Party/SyntropicOS).
  3. Configure Include Paths:
  4. Right-click your project → Properties → C/C++ Build → Settings → MCU GCC Compiler → Include paths.
  5. Add ${workspace_loc:/${ProjName}/Middlewares/Third_Party/SyntropicOS/src}.
  6. Ensure ${workspace_loc:/${ProjName}/Core/Inc} is also in the include path (where your syn_config.h will reside).
  7. Add Source Folders to Build:
  8. Right-click Middlewares/Third_Party/SyntropicOS/src/syntropic → Source Actions → Add to Build (ensure src/syntropic/port_stubs/syn_port_stubs.c is included).
  9. For STM32Cube HAL projects, also include src/port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.c (and include port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.h in main.c for SYN_PORT_STM32_PIN() and syn_port_stm32_register_uart()).
  10. Set C Standard:
  11. In MCU GCC Compiler → Miscellaneous, set C Language Standard to -std=c99.
  12. Configuration Header:
  13. Copy src/syntropic/syn_config_template.h to your project's Core/Inc/syn_config.h.

docs.title: PlatformIO Integration
docs.text:
SyntropicOS is a native PlatformIO library (library.json). Include it directly via lib_deps in your platformio.ini:

[env:stm32f407]
platform = ststm32
board = disco_f407vg
framework = stm32cube
build_flags =
    -std=c99
lib_deps =
    SyntropicOS

Or reference the Git repository directly:

lib_deps =
    https://github.com/outlookhazy/SyntropicOS.git

docs.title: CMake + VS Code Cortex-Debug
docs.text:
1. CMakeLists.txt: 

    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(my_embedded_app C)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 99)

add_subdirectory(lib/SyntropicOS)
add_executable(my_app
    src/main.c
    lib/SyntropicOS/src/port/stm32_hal/port_stm32_hal.c
)
target_include_directories(my_app PRIVATE include)
target_compile_definitions(my_app PRIVATE STM32F4xx)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE syntropic syn_stubs)

  2. .vscode/launch.json (Cortex-Debug ST-Link): 

    {
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Cortex-Debug (ST-Link)",
      "type": "cortex-debug",
      "request": "launch",
      "servertype": "openocd",
      "executable": "${workspaceRoot}/build/my_app.elf",
      "device": "STM32F407VG",
      "configFiles": [
        "interface/stlink.cfg",
        "target/stm32f4x.cfg"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text:
1. Add Group & Files:
  2. In the Project Workspace tree, right-click target → Add Group... → Name it SyntropicOS.
  3. Right-click SyntropicOS group → Add Existing Files to Group 'SyntropicOS'.
  4. Select the .c files from src/syntropic/ module subdirectories (audio, ble, cli, control, crypto, debug, display, drivers, dsp, input, log, motor, net, output, proto, sched, sensor, storage, system, ui, util, vm).
  5. Set Include Paths:
  6. Click Options for Target (Alt+F7) → C/C++ tab.
  7. In Include Paths, add: ..\SyntropicOS\src; ..\Core\Inc;
  8. Compiler Options:
  9. Check C99 Mode in the C/C++ tab.
  10. syntropic.h automatically includes syn_config.h from your include path via __has_include("syn_config.h") (add --preinclude=syn_config.h if translation units include individual module headers directly without syntropic.h).
  11. SysTick & Critical Sections:
  12. Ensure SysTick_Handler in stm32f4xx_it.c increments HAL_IncTick() or syn_port_get_tick_ms().

docs.title: Library Installation
docs.text:
SyntropicOS is packaged as a standard Arduino Library (library.properties).

  1. Installation Methods:
  2. Library Manager: Search for SyntropicOS in Sketch → Include Library → Manage Libraries...
  3. Add .ZIP Library: Download repository release ZIP → Sketch → Include Library → Add .ZIP Library...

  4. Manual Placement: Extract into your sketchbook libraries/ directory (Arduino/libraries/SyntropicOS).

  5. Header Inclusion & Sketch Usage:

  6. Include <SyntropicOS.h> in your .ino sketch and drive the scheduler from loop(): 
    #include <SyntropicOS.h>

static SYN_Task tasks[1];
static SYN_Sched sched;

static SYN_PT_Status blink_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        syn_gpio_toggle(LED_BUILTIN);
        PT_TASK_DELAY_MS(pt, task, 500);
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

void setup() {
    syn_gpio_init(LED_BUILTIN, SYN_GPIO_OUTPUT);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[0], "blink", blink_task, SYN_PRIO_NORMAL, NULL);
    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 1);
}

void loop() {
    syn_sched_run(&sched);
}

docs.title: Porting Guide
docs.text:
SyntropicOS isolates hardware-specific code behind a thin C99 port layer. Portable modules under src/syntropic/ never touch MCU registers directly; instead, they call syn_port_* functions declared in src/syntropic/port/ (and src/port/ for Ethernet/USB MAC contracts).

If your target is already covered by a Reference Port, add that port .c file to your build instead of writing one from scratch.

docs.title: System Port Example (Nested Critical Sections & Tick Source)
docs.text:
syn_port_enter_critical() and syn_port_exit_critical() must support nesting and must preserve the caller's interrupt mask state (so calling a critical section from inside an ISR does not prematurely unmask interrupts on exit). Complete Cortex-M / STM32 HAL pattern:

#include "syntropic/port/syn_port_system.h"
#include "stm32f4xx_hal.h"

static volatile uint32_t s_crit_depth = 0U;
static volatile uint32_t s_saved_primask = 0U;

void syn_port_enter_critical(void) {
    uint32_t primask = __get_PRIMASK();
    __disable_irq();
    if (s_crit_depth == 0U) {
        s_saved_primask = primask;
    }
    s_crit_depth++;
}

void syn_port_exit_critical(void) {
    SYN_COMPILER_BARRIER();
    if (s_crit_depth > 0U) {
        s_crit_depth--;
        if (s_crit_depth == 0U && (s_saved_primask & 1U) == 0U) {
            __enable_irq();
        }
    }
}

uint32_t syn_port_get_tick_ms(void) {
    return HAL_GetTick();
}

uint32_t syn_port_get_tick_us(void) {
    return HAL_GetTick() * 1000U; /* Or interpolate SysTick->VAL; see port_stm32_hal.c */
}

void syn_port_delay_ms(uint32_t ms) {
    HAL_Delay(ms);
}

SYN_NORETURN void syn_port_system_reset(void) {
    NVIC_SystemReset();
    for (;;) {}
}

docs.title: Weak Stubs (syn_port_stubs.c)
docs.text:
Compile src/syntropic/port_stubs/syn_port_stubs.c (or link syn_stubs in CMake / $(SYN_STUB_SRCS) in Make) alongside your port file. Every syn_port_* symbol has a SYN_WEAK fallback that invokes syn_assert_failed(__FILE__, __LINE__). Your strong definitions override the stubs automatically, while any unimplemented port function you accidentally call traps deterministically at runtime instead of failing to link unused modules.

target_link_libraries(your_target PRIVATE syntropic syn_stubs)

docs.title: Testing & Verification Guide
docs.text: SyntropicOS features a multi-tiered test and quality assurance architecture ranging from ultra-fast host-side unit testing to containerized 3rd-party daemon integration, QEMU bare-metal CPU emulation, protocol fuzzing, sanitizers, and static analysis.

docs.title: Containerized Testing Workflow
docs.text:
All verification targets are invoked from the root of a SyntropicOS repository checkout and run inside an isolated Podman or Docker image (syntropicos-test). Every make container-* target automatically builds syntropicos-test from tools/containers/Containerfile on first run. Omit the container- prefix only when already inside the container or using an equivalent native toolchain.

Containerized Target In-Container / Native Target Description make container-test make test Runs Unity unit test suite & LCOV coverage make container-format make format Checks C99 formatting via clang-format (FIX=1 to apply) make container-lint make lint Runs clang-tidy AST linter & protothread switch / cross-yield local checks make container-san make san Executes unit tests under AddressSanitizer (ASan) & UBSan make container-qemu make qemu Bare-metal QEMU ARM Cortex-M4 test suite & deterministic -icount chunk-budget gate make container-renode make renode Renode STM32F4 board-level peripheral emulation make container-examples make examples Cross-compiles all examples & lean syn_config.h profiles make container-fuzz make fuzz Runs LLVM libFuzzer protocol targets make container-cov make cov Generates LCOV line and branch coverage summaries (build/cov/coverage_src.info) make container-static make static Performs Cppcheck and Clang scan-build static analysis make container-dox make dox Builds Doxygen API documentation and enforces zero warnings make container-integration make integration Executes E2E tests against containerized 3rd-party service daemons

docs.title: Technical Architecture & Memory Guarantees
docs.text: Property Guarantee Standards Compliance Pure C99, compatible with GCC, Clang, IAR, Keil, and MSVC. Heap Allocation 0 Bytes. No malloc(), free(), or dynamic memory pools. Concurrency Model Cooperative stackless coroutines (syn_pt). RAM footprint = 2 bytes/thread. Reentrancy & Safety Lock-free SPSC data structures for safe ISR ↔ Task communication.

docs.title: Module Overview & Catalog
docs.text: SyntropicOS ships 278 portable C99 module headers across 23 categories under src/syntropic/, backed by 24 core platform port contracts (src/syntropic/port/) and 3 optional MAC/USB controller contracts (src/port/). Every module uses static, caller-owned state structures with zero heap allocation (malloc/free are never called).

docs.title: Including Modules & Trimming Firmware Size
docs.text:
• Umbrella Header: #include <syntropic/syntropic.h> pulls in all enabled subsystem headers (controlled by syn_config.h).
  • Targeted Header: #include <syntropic/<category>/syn_<name>.h> includes a single module directly for faster incremental builds or standalone modules.
  • Compile-Time Pruning: Copy src/syntropic/syn_config_template.h to syn_config.h on your include path to disable unused SYN_USE_* switches or tune static table bounds. Pair with -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections and -Wl,--gc-sections so the linker strips unreferenced functions even when building the full source tree.

docs.title: SyntropicOS Embedded Audio Subsystem (src/syntropic/audio/)
docs.text: The SyntropicOS Audio Subsystem provides lightweight, zero-heap, integer-only audio codecs and PCM streaming engine for microcontrollers.

docs.title: IMA-ADPCM Codec (syn_adpcm)
docs.text:
• Compression: 4:1 lossy compression (16-bit linear PCM <-> 4-bit ADPCM nibbles).
  • Footprint: ~200 bytes code, ~8 bytes state (SYN_ADPCM_State).
  • Compatibility: Standard WAV IMA-ADPCM format (ffmpeg, Audacity compatible).

docs.title: Bluetooth SBC Decoder (syn_sbc)
docs.text:
• Specification: Bluetooth SIG A2DP Sub-Band Codec spec compliant.
  • Subbands: 4 and 8 subbands, 4/8/12/16 blocks.
  • Modes: Mono, Dual Channel, Stereo, Joint Stereo.

docs.title: PCM Streaming Playback Engine (syn_audio)
docs.text:
• Double-Buffering: Ping-pong PCM buffer (SYN_Audio, syn_audio_init, syn_audio_start, syn_audio_feed) preventing audio underrun.
  • ISR Hooks: Decoupled syn_audio_isr_half() and syn_audio_isr_complete() handlers.

docs.title: Multi-Channel PCM Audio Mixer (syn_audio_mixer)
docs.text: • Polyphonic Mixing (audio/syn_audio_mixer.h, SYN_USE_AUDIO): Blends up to SYN_AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_CHANNELS (4U default) 16-bit PCM streams into a single output buffer (syn_audio_mixer_render) with per-channel (syn_audio_mixer_play, syn_audio_mixer_set_channel_volume) and master (syn_audio_mixer_set_master_volume) Q15 gain scaling (SYN_AUDIO_GAIN_UNITY = 32768U), looping, and saturating clamp.

docs.title: RIFF / WAVE Container Parser (syn_wav)
docs.text: • Zero-Copy Header Parsing (audio/syn_wav.h, SYN_USE_AUDIO): syn_wav_parse_header() inspects in-memory RIFF/WAVE containers (SYN_WAV_Info) to extract sample rate, channel count, bit depth, payload offset, and total sample count for linear PCM (SYN_WAV_FORMAT_PCM) and IMA-ADPCM (SYN_WAV_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM) assets.

docs.title: Voice Activity Detector (syn_vad)
docs.text:
• Algorithms: Multi-feature acoustic onset/voice detector:
  • Short-Time Energy (STE)
  • Zero-Crossing Rate (ZCR)
  • High-Frequency Differential Energy (HFDE)
  • Noise Tracking: Adaptive background noise floor tracking via Exponential Moving Average (EMA).
  • Hysteresis: Configurable attack frame threshold (attack_frames) and hangover release timing (hangover_frames).
  • Presets: SYN_VAD_SENSITIVITY_SENSITIVE, SYN_VAD_SENSITIVITY_NORMAL, SYN_VAD_SENSITIVITY_AGGRESSIVE.
#include <syntropic/audio/syn_vad.h>

static SYN_VAD vad;

void vad_setup(void) {
    SYN_VAD_Config cfg = {
        .sample_rate_hz = 16000U,
        .frame_length = 160U, /* 10 ms frame */
        .sensitivity = SYN_VAD_SENSITIVITY_NORMAL,
        .attack_frames = 2U,
        .hangover_frames = 10U,
    };
    syn_vad_init(&vad, &cfg);
}

void process_audio_frame(const int16_t *pcm_samples, size_t count) {
    SYN_VAD_State state = syn_vad_process_frame(&vad, pcm_samples, count, NULL);
    if (state == SYN_VAD_STATE_SPEECH) {
        /* Wake wake-word detector or stream to ASR / cloud */
    }
}

docs.title: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Host Stack
docs.text: The SyntropicOS BLE module (syn_ble) provides a zero-heap, deterministic Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) host stack for microcontrollers paired with external BLE controllers over UART (H:4) or SPI.

docs.title: Header Reference
docs.text: Header Layer Description ble/syn_ble_hci.h HCI Transport H:4 UART/SPI framing for HCI Command (0x01), ACL Data (0x02), and Event (0x04) packets (SYN_BLE_HCI, syn_ble_hci_init, syn_ble_hci_rx_byte) ble/syn_ble_l2cap.h L2CAP Connection-oriented CID 0x0004 (ATT) fragmentation and reassembly (SYN_BLE_L2CAP, syn_ble_l2cap_init) ble/syn_ble_att.h ATT Attribute Protocol PDU encoder and decoder (SYN_BLE_ATT_*, Read/Write/FindInfo/ReadByGroupType/HandleValueNotification) ble/syn_ble_gap.h GAP Peripheral advertising, central scanning, and connection lifecycle (SYN_BLE_GAP, syn_ble_gap_init, syn_ble_gap_set_adv_data) ble/syn_ble_gatt.h GATT Server Static attribute table dispatch, per-connection CCCD state, and outbound notifications (SYN_BLE_GATT, syn_ble_gatt_init, syn_ble_gatt_notify) port/syn_port_ble_hci.h Port HAL Platform controller transport (syn_port_ble_hci_tx, syn_port_ble_hci_reset)

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Zero Dynamic Memory: All HCI RX reassembly buffers, L2CAP connection tables, and GATT attribute entries are statically allocated.
  • H:4 Transport Layer: Compliance with Bluetooth Core Specification Vol 4, Part A.
  • GATT Server: Static attribute tables for custom or standard SIG services and characteristics, with independent per-connection CCCD tracking.
  • GAP Peripheral & Central: Connectable and non-connectable advertising, active/passive scanning, and connection parameter updates.

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/syntropic.h>

static SYN_BLE_HCI hci;
static SYN_BLE_GAP gap;
static SYN_BLE_GATT gatt;

/* Define GATT attribute table */
static const SYN_BLE_GATT_Attr gatt_table[] = {
    { 0x0001, SYN_BLE_UUID_PRIMARY_SERVICE, SYN_BLE_PROP_READ, NULL, NULL, (const uint8_t *)"\x09\x18", 2 },
    { 0x0002, 0x2A6E, SYN_BLE_PROP_READ, temp_read_cb, NULL, NULL, 0 }
};

void ble_init(SYN_BLE_HCI_EventCb hci_evt_cb, SYN_BLE_HCI_AclCb hci_acl_cb,
              SYN_BLE_GAP_EventCb gap_evt_cb) {
    SYN_BLE_HCI_Config hci_cfg = {
        .evt_cb = hci_evt_cb,
        .acl_cb = hci_acl_cb,
        .user_data = NULL,
    };
    syn_ble_hci_init(&hci, &hci_cfg);
    syn_ble_gap_init(&gap, &hci, gap_evt_cb, NULL);
    syn_ble_gatt_init(&gatt, gatt_table, 2, NULL);
}

docs.title: 1. COBS & Packet Router Pipeline (syn_cobs + syn_router)
docs.text: For MCU-to-MCU serial communication over UART TTL or RS232/RS485, SyntropicOS pairs COBS Framing with the Addressed Router.

docs.title: Pipeline Data Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    UART["Single-Byte UART RX Interrupt"] --> Decoder["syn_cobs_decoder_feed"]
    Decoder -->|0x00 Delimiter Found| Assembly["Decoded Frame Buffer"]
    Assembly --> Router["syn_router_poll"]
    Router -->|Match Node ID & Msg Type| Callback["Handler Callback (e.g. on_led_command)"]

docs.title: Complete STM32 HAL UART Single-Byte Interrupt Example
docs.text:
#include <string.h>
#include <syntropic/proto/syn_cobs.h>
#include <syntropic/net/syn_router.h>

#define MASTER_NODE_ID 0x01
#define SLAVE_NODE_ID  0x02
#define MSG_TYPE_LED   0x10

static uint8_t rx_byte;
static SYN_COBS_Decoder cobs_dec;
static uint8_t cobs_buf[128];

static uint8_t rx_pkt_buf[128];
static volatile size_t rx_pkt_len;
static volatile bool rx_pkt_ready;

static SYN_Router router;
static SYN_RouterHandler handlers[4];

// Custom Transport: Send framed COBS packet over UART
static bool uart_send(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    uint8_t enc[140];
    size_t enc_len = syn_cobs_encode(data, len, enc);
    enc[enc_len++] = 0x00; // Append 0x00 frame delimiter

    return HAL_UART_Transmit(&huart2, enc, (uint16_t)enc_len, 100) == HAL_OK;
}

// Custom Transport: Poll decoded COBS frame buffered from ISR
static bool uart_recv(uint8_t *data, size_t max_len, size_t *out_len, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (!rx_pkt_ready) {
        return false;
    }
    size_t n = rx_pkt_len;
    if (n > max_len) {
        rx_pkt_ready = false;
        return false;
    }
    memcpy(data, rx_pkt_buf, n);
    *out_len = n;
    rx_pkt_ready = false;
    return true;
}

static SYN_Transport transport = { .send = uart_send, .recv = uart_recv, .ctx = NULL };

// COBS Decoder Callback when a complete frame arrives
static void on_cobs_frame(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (!rx_pkt_ready && len <= sizeof(rx_pkt_buf)) {
        memcpy(rx_pkt_buf, data, len);
        rx_pkt_len = len;
        rx_pkt_ready = true;
    }
}

// Single-Byte UART Interrupt Callback (No DMA)
void HAL_UART_RxCpltCallback(UART_HandleTypeDef *huart) {
    if (huart->Instance == USART2) {
        syn_cobs_decoder_feed(&cobs_dec, rx_byte);
        HAL_UART_Receive_IT(&huart2, &rx_byte, 1); // Re-arm interrupt
    }
}

// Message Handler Callback
static void on_led_command(const SYN_Packet *pkt, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (pkt->len > 0 && pkt->payload[0] == 0x01) {
        HAL_GPIO_WritePin(GPIOA, GPIO_PIN_5, GPIO_PIN_SET); // LED ON
    }
}

void app_init(void) {
    syn_cobs_decoder_init(&cobs_dec, cobs_buf, sizeof(cobs_buf), on_cobs_frame, NULL);

    syn_router_init(&router, SLAVE_NODE_ID, &transport, handlers, 4);
    syn_router_register(&router, MSG_TYPE_LED, on_led_command, NULL);

    HAL_UART_Receive_IT(&huart2, &rx_byte, 1);
}

void app_loop(void) {
    syn_router_poll(&router);
}

docs.title: 2. M-Bus Protocol (syn_mbus.h)
docs.text: The M-Bus (Meter-Bus) driver supports utility metering devices (water, gas, electricity, heat meters) compliant with EN 13757-2 / EN 13757-3.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Single-byte ACK (0xE5) parsing.
  • Short frame (0x10) and Long frame (0x68) header validation.
  • Arithmetic checksum calculation and byte-at-a-time streaming parser.
#include <syntropic/proto/syn_mbus.h>

void parse_mbus_stream(const uint8_t *buffer, size_t len) {
    SYN_MBUS_Frame frame;
    if (syn_mbus_decode_frame(buffer, len, &frame) == SYN_OK) {
        printf("M-Bus Frame Received! C-Field: 0x%02X, Address: 0x%02X\n",
               frame.c_field, frame.a_field);
    }
}

docs.title: 3. BACnet MS/TP Protocol (syn_bacnet.h)
docs.text: The BACnet MS/TP protocol engine implements ANSI/ASHRAE 135 / ISO 16484-5 token-passing serial communication over RS485 without dynamic memory allocation (malloc).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• MS/TP Framing & CRC: Encodes/decodes Preamble (0x55 0xFF), Header CRC-8, and Data CRC-16 (ANSI X3.28 polynomial).
  • APDU Services: Supports Who-Is / I-Am unconfirmed services and ReadProperty / WriteProperty confirmed services.
  • Static Object Database: Manages Device, Analog Input (AI), Analog Output (AO), Binary Input (BI), and Binary Output (BO) objects.
#include <syntropic/proto/syn_bacnet.h>

static SYN_BACnet_Node node;

void setup_bacnet(void) {
    syn_bacnet_node_init(&node, 12, 123456); // MAC 12, Device ID 123456
    syn_bacnet_add_object(&node, SYN_BACNET_OBJ_ANALOG_INPUT, 1, 23.5f, "Temperature");
}

docs.title: 4. DALI Protocol (syn_dali.h)
docs.text: The DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface / IEC 62386-101/102) engine implements Master and Control Gear (Slave) lighting nodes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Manchester Encoding/Decoding: Bi-phase bit encoding/decoding helper functions.
  • Forward & Backward Frames: 16-bit Master Forward Frame decoding (syn_dali_decode_forward) and 8-bit Slave Backward Frame encoding (syn_dali_encode_backward).
  • Direct Arc Power Control (DAPC): Manages logarithmic/linear arc dimming levels (0..254), min/max bounds, power-on levels, and system failure levels.

docs.title: 5. Modbus RTU Master & Slave (syn_modbus.h, syn_modbus_master.h)
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides non-blocking state-machine drivers for Modbus RTU Slave (proto/syn_modbus.h), Modbus RTU Master (proto/syn_modbus_master.h), and Modbus TCP MBAP ADU framing (proto/syn_modbus_tcp.h).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Non-blocking State Machine: Processing occurs without thread blocking via periodic polling (syn_modbus_process / syn_modbus_master_process).
  • Inter-Frame Silence (t3.5): Timing gap detection handles partial frame arrival cleanly over UART DMA / ring buffers.
  • Modbus TCP (proto/syn_modbus_tcp.h): Encodes and decodes 7-byte MBAP headers (SYN_MBAP_Header, syn_mbap_encode_header, syn_mbap_decode_header) and wraps Slave/Client ADUs (syn_modbus_tcp_process_slave, syn_modbus_tcp_build_client_adu).

docs.title: 6. Zero-Heap Ethernet & IP Protocol Suite (syn_eth, syn_dhcp, syn_icmp, syn_autoip, syn_netcfg)
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides a standalone, zero-heap Ethernet II, TCP/UDP/IPv4, TLS/DTLS 1.3, and application networking stack engineered for embedded microcontrollers.

docs.title: Core Link, IP & Transport Sub-Modules
docs.text:
• Zero-Copy Packet Buffer Pool (net/syn_netbuf.h): Reference-counted packet buffers (SYN_NetBuf, SYN_NetBufPool, syn_netbuf_alloc, syn_netbuf_push, syn_netbuf_free) avoiding per-layer payload copies.
  • Ethernet II & ARP (net/syn_eth.h): Raw Ethernet II framing, MAC address filtering, and configurable static ARP table cache (SYN_ETH_ARP_CACHE_SIZE, defaults to 8 entries).
  • Native TCP Engine (net/syn_tcp.h): Zero-alloc IPv4 TCP state machine (SYN_TCP_LISTEN, SYN_TCP_SYN_RCVD, SYN_TCP_ESTABLISHED, SYN_TCP_FIN_WAIT), 3-way handshake (SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK), sequence/ACK tracking, and non-blocking PT_TCP_BLOCK_READ protothread task macro.
  • Native UDP Engine (net/syn_udp.h): Zero-alloc IPv4 UDP demuxing stack, 8-byte header construction, pseudo-header checksum (syn_udp_checksum), targeted destination port waking (syn_task_resume), and PT_UDP_BLOCK_READ protothread macro.
  • Pluggable Transport & Socket Bridges (net/syn_transport.h, net/syn_transport_tcp.h, net/syn_transport_udp.h): Generic SYN_Transport byte-stream/datagram vtable (syn_transport_send, syn_transport_recv), TCP socket adapter (SYN_TransportTcp, syn_transport_tcp_init), and UDP dual-stack bridge connecting syn_port_udp_* to syn_udp.
  • DHCP Client (net/syn_dhcp.h): RFC 2131 BOOTP/DHCP client state machine (DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST → ACK) over UDP ports 67/68.
  • ICMP & IGMPv2 (net/syn_icmp.h, net/syn_igmp.h): RFC 792 ICMP Echo Request / Reply (Ping) engine (SYN_USE_ICMP) and RFC 2236 IGMPv2 IPv4 multicast group join/leave/report engine (SYN_USE_IGMP, syn_igmp_join_group, syn_igmp_leave_group).
  • RFC 3927 AutoIP (net/syn_autoip.h): Link-Local 169.254.x.x address selection, ARP probing, and collision recovery.
  • Network IP Manager (net/syn_netcfg.h): Unified IP configuration manager supporting Static IP, DHCP, automatic AutoIP fallback, and physical Link Up / Link Down state transitions.

docs.title: Security, Naming, Time & Application Sub-Modules (net/*.h)
7. Unified Diagnostic Services (UDS / ISO 14229 & ISO 15765-2) (syn_uds.h, syn_isotp.h)
docs.text: SyntropicOS includes a zero-heap UDS ISO 14229 diagnostic server engine operating over CAN / ISO 15765-2 transport.

docs.title: 0x11 ECU Reset Deferred Integration
docs.text:
When handling 0x11 ECUReset requests, the ECU must transmit the positive ACK payload (0x51 <sub-function>) over CAN/ISO-TP before resetting the MCU hardware.

SyntropicOS provides native deferred post-TX reset callbacks with a configurable delay window (50 ms default):

#include <syntropic/proto/syn_uds.h>

static SYN_UDS_Server g_uds;

static void on_ecu_reset(uint8_t reset_type, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    switch (reset_type) {
    case SYN_UDS_RESET_HARD:
    case SYN_UDS_RESET_KEY_OFF_ON:
    case SYN_UDS_RESET_SOFT:
    default:
        syn_port_system_reset(); /* Trigger hardware system reset 50 ms after 0x51 response */
        break;
    }
}

void uds_init(void) {
    syn_uds_init(&g_uds);
    syn_uds_set_reset_handler(&g_uds, on_ecu_reset, NULL);
    syn_uds_set_reset_wait_ms(&g_uds, 50); /* 50 ms post-TX delay window */
}

void uds_task_10ms(uint32_t dt_ms) {
    syn_uds_tick(&g_uds, dt_ms); /* Automatically triggers on_ecu_reset callback after 50 ms */
}

docs.title: Per-DID Session & Security Authorization Filters
docs.text:
DIDs can be registered with explicit session and security level bitmask filters using syn_uds_register_did_ext:

uint8_t engine_speed[2];
/* Register DID 0xF190 accessible in DEFAULT/EXTENDED sessions and SECURITY LEVEL 1 */
syn_uds_register_did_ext(&g_uds, 0xF190, engine_speed, sizeof(engine_speed), true,
                         SYN_UDS_SESSION_MASK_DEFAULT | SYN_UDS_SESSION_MASK_EXTENDED,
                         SYN_UDS_SECURITY_MASK_LEVEL_1);

docs.title: Addressing Mode Support (Physical vs. Functional)
docs.text:
ISO 14229-1 mandates differentiation between Physical (1:1 point-to-point) and Functional (1:N broadcast) CAN addressing modes:

  • SYN_UDS_ADDR_PHYSICAL: Point-to-point requests. Positively or negatively responded to as per protocol rules.
  • SYN_UDS_ADDR_FUNCTIONAL: Broadcast requests. Functional-supported services (0x10, 0x11, 0x14, 0x19, 0x22, 0x28, 0x29, 0x31, 0x3E, 0x83, 0x85, 0x87) are processed; physical-only services (0x23, 0x24, 0x27, 0x2A, 0x2C, 0x2E, 0x2F, 0x34, 0x35, 0x36, 0x37, 0x38, 0x3D, 0x84, 0x86) are silently dropped (resp_len = 0). Standard negative responses (0x11, 0x12, 0x7E) on functional requests are suppressed to prevent bus flooding.
/* Processing a physical UDS request */
syn_uds_process_request(&g_uds, req_buf, req_len, resp_buf, sizeof(resp_buf), &resp_len, SYN_UDS_ADDR_PHYSICAL);

/* Processing a functional broadcast request */
syn_uds_process_request(&g_uds, req_buf, req_len, resp_buf, sizeof(resp_buf), &resp_len, SYN_UDS_ADDR_FUNCTIONAL);

docs.title: Per-Service Session & Security Policy Overrides
docs.text:
Configure custom session permission masks or required security levels for top-level Service Identifiers (SIDs):

/* Restrict ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22) to EXTENDED session */
syn_uds_set_service_session_mask(&g_uds, 0x22, SYN_UDS_SESSION_MASK_EXTENDED);

/* Require Security Level 1 before ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22) can be executed */
syn_uds_set_service_security_mask(&g_uds, 0x22, SYN_UDS_SECURITY_MASK_LEVEL_1);

docs.title: AccessTimingParameter (0x83) Callback Handler
docs.text:
Register a callback handler to monitor or override P2Server_max and P2*Server_max timing parameters for Service 0x83 subfunctions (0x01 Read Extended, 0x02 Set Default, 0x03 Read Active, 0x04 Set Given):

static bool on_access_timing(SYN_UDS_AccessTimingType timing_type, uint16_t *p2_max_ms,
                             uint16_t *p2_star_max_10ms, void *ctx)
{
    (void)ctx;
    switch (timing_type) {
    case SYN_UDS_TIMING_READ_EXTENDED:
    case SYN_UDS_TIMING_READ_ACTIVE:
        if (p2_max_ms != NULL) *p2_max_ms = 50U;         /* 50 ms */
        if (p2_star_max_10ms != NULL) *p2_star_max_10ms = 500U; /* 5000 ms */
        return true;
    case SYN_UDS_TIMING_SET_TO_DEFAULT:
        if (p2_max_ms != NULL) *p2_max_ms = 50U;
        if (p2_star_max_10ms != NULL) *p2_star_max_10ms = 500U;
        return true;
    case SYN_UDS_TIMING_SET_TO_GIVEN:
        return (p2_max_ms != NULL && *p2_max_ms >= 10U);
    default:
        return false;
    }
}

/* Register handler on UDS server context */
syn_uds_register_access_timing(&g_uds, on_access_timing, NULL);

docs.title: Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) Management & ISO 14229-1 Lifecycle
docs.text:
SyntropicOS implements normative ISO 14229-1 DTC status bit management, fault detection counters, and operation cycle boundaries directly in the core stack:

  • Normative State Machine: Tracks DTCStatusByte bits (testFailed, testFailedThisOperationCycle, pendingDTC, confirmedDTC, testNotCompletedSinceLastClear, testFailedSinceLastClear, testNotCompletedThisOperationCycle).
  • Single Source of Truth: The core SYN_UDS_Server context manages status bits and fault detection counters (-128 to +127). Applications should not duplicate status byte tracking.
  • OEM Extension Hook (dtc_cb): Snapshot DIDs (subfunction 0x04) and Extended Data records (subfunction 0x06) are defined by vehicle manufacturers and delegated cleanly via syn_uds_register_dtc_handler().
/* 1. Registration at initialization */
syn_uds_register_dtc(&g_uds, 0x00B10016U, 0x00, SYN_UDS_DTC_SEVERITY_CHECK_IMMEDIATELY);

/* 2. Diagnostic monitors report test results (pass / fail) */
syn_uds_dtc_report_test_result(&g_uds, 0x00B10016U, true);  /* Sets testFailed, pending, confirmed; FDC = +127 */
syn_uds_dtc_report_test_result(&g_uds, 0x00B10016U, false); /* Clears testFailed; FDC = -128 */

/* 3. Driving / Operation cycle boundary */
syn_uds_dtc_start_operation_cycle(&g_uds); /* Resets testFailedThisOpCycle; clears pendingDTC if cycle completed clean */

/* 4. Querying authoritative status & SAE J2012 string formatting (proto/syn_uds_util.h) */
uint8_t dtc_status = 0;
char dtc_str[6];
syn_uds_dtc_get_status(&g_uds, 0x00B10016U, &dtc_status);
syn_uds_dtc_to_str(0x00B10016U, dtc_str); /* Formats "B1001" / parses via syn_uds_dtc_from_str() */

docs.title: 8. DoIP Protocol Stack (syn_doip)
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides a zero-malloc ISO 13400-2 Diagnostic over IP (DoIP) transport layer for automotive Ethernet diagnostics.

docs.title: DoIP Features & Characteristics
docs.text:
• 8-Byte Header Serialization: Big-endian packing for Protocol Version (0x02), Inverse Protocol Version (0xFD), 2-byte Payload Type, and 4-byte Payload Length.
  • Vehicle Discovery & Identification: Supports UDP Vehicle Identification Requests (0x0001/0x0002/0x0003) and responds with Vehicle Announcement Messages (0x0004) containing VIN, EID (MAC), GID, and logical address.
  • Routing Activation: Handles TCP Routing Activation Requests (0x0005) and returns Routing Activation Responses (0x0006).
  • UDS Message Dispatch: Unpacks TCP Diagnostic Messages (0x8001), validates target logical address, passes UDS payload directly to syn_uds_process_request(), and frames positive response / NACK frames (0x8002/0x8003).

docs.title: Example Integration
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/proto/syn_doip.h>
#include <syntropic/proto/syn_uds.h>

static SYN_DoIP_Server g_doip;
static SYN_UDS_Server g_uds;

void doip_setup(void)
{
    syn_uds_init(&g_uds);
    syn_doip_init(&g_doip, 0x1001); /* Logical Address 0x1001 */

    uint8_t vin[17] = "SYNTROPICOS123456";
    uint8_t eid[6]  = {0x00, 0x80, 0xE1, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03};
    uint8_t gid[6]  = {0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF};
    syn_doip_set_identifiers(&g_doip, vin, eid, gid);
}

void on_socket_rx(const uint8_t *rx_buf, uint16_t rx_len, uint8_t *tx_buf, uint16_t max_tx, uint16_t *tx_len)
{
    syn_doip_process_msg(&g_doip, &g_uds, rx_buf, rx_len, tx_buf, max_tx, tx_len);
}

docs.title: 9. DNS-Based Service Discovery (syn_dnssd)
docs.text: Cleanroom multicast DNS-SD responder (RFC 6763 / RFC 6762) on UDP port 5353 (224.0.0.251) providing zero-allocation service advertisement.

docs.title: DNS-SD Features
docs.text:
• Resource Records: Automatic encoding of PTR (service type), SRV (port + hostname), TXT (attributes), and A (IPv4) records.
  • Gratuitous Announcement: syn_dnssd_announce() broadcasts multicast announcements on service registration.
  • Query Demuxing: syn_dnssd_process_query() matches incoming queries and replies with authoritative response packets.
  • Active Service Browsing: syn_dnssd_browser_init() and cooperative protothread coroutine syn_dnssd_browse_task() query and stream discovered nodes to application callbacks.
#include <syntropic/net/syn_dnssd.h>

static SYN_DnsSd g_dnssd;
static SYN_DnsSd_Browser g_browser;

static void on_node_found(const SYN_DnsSd_Discovered *svc, void *user_data) {
    printf("Discovered %s on %d.%d.%d.%d:%u (host: %s, txt: %s)\n",
           svc->instance_name, svc->ip[0], svc->ip[1], svc->ip[2], svc->ip[3],
           svc->port, svc->hostname, svc->txt);
}

void dnssd_setup(void) {
    syn_dnssd_init(&g_dnssd);

    /* 1. Register and announce local service */
    SYN_DnsSd_Service svc = {
        .instance_name = "Syntropic Sensor Node",
        .service_type = "_http._tcp",
        .hostname = "sensor-node",
        .port = 80,
        .ip = {192, 168, 1, 150},
        .txt_records = {"version=1.0", "vendor=Syntropic"},
        .txt_count = 2
    };
    syn_dnssd_register(&g_dnssd, &svc);

    uint8_t buf[1024];
    size_t len = 0;
    syn_dnssd_announce(&g_dnssd, 0, buf, sizeof(buf), &len);

    /* 2. Start cooperative service discovery browser (5-second window) */
    syn_dnssd_browser_init(&g_browser, &g_dnssd, "_coap._udp", on_node_found, NULL, 5000);
}

docs.title: 10. OMA LwM2M Client & Autonomous Supervisor (proto/syn_lwm2m.h, proto/syn_lwm2m_task.h)
docs.text:
proto/syn_lwm2m.h (SYN_USE_LWM2M) implements the zero-heap OMA LwM2M v1.1/v1.2 client object tree (SYN_LwM2M_Client, SYN_LwM2M_Object), TLV and Core Link-Format encoders (syn_lwm2m_tlv_encode_*), and IPSO Device/Sensor object builders. proto/syn_lwm2m_task.h (SYN_USE_LWM2M_TASK) wraps the client in an event-driven supervisor task managing the complete connection lifecycle: - Autonomous Registration: Initial registration with core Link-Format serialization (</3/0>, </5/0>, </3303/0>). - Autonomous Lifetime Renewal: Automatic update requests dispatched when reaching 80% of configured lifetime_s. - RFC 7641 Observe & Notify: Periodic evaluation of resource changes with pmin suppression and pmax expiry. - DTLS 1.3 Integration: Cooperative TLS/DTLS handshake advancement via SYN_CoapsClient. - System Hook Routing: Automatic invocation of reboot, factory reset, and OTA firmware update handlers.

#include <syntropic/proto/syn_lwm2m_task.h>

static SYN_LwM2M_Client g_client;
static SYN_LwM2M_Task g_task;
static SYN_LwM2M_DeviceContext g_dev_ctx;
static SYN_LwM2M_SensorContext g_temp_ctx;
static SYN_LwM2M_Object g_dev_obj;
static SYN_LwM2M_Object g_temp_obj;

static uint8_t g_rx_scratch[512];
static uint8_t g_tx_scratch[512];

static void on_reboot(void *user_data) {
    (void)user_data;
    syn_port_system_reset();
}

void lwm2m_app_init(SYN_Transport *transport) {
    syn_lwm2m_client_init(&g_client, "syn-edge-01", 300U, transport);

    g_dev_obj = syn_lwm2m_make_device_object(&g_dev_ctx);
    g_temp_obj = syn_lwm2m_make_temperature_object(&g_temp_ctx);
    syn_lwm2m_register_object(&g_client, &g_dev_obj);
    syn_lwm2m_register_object(&g_client, &g_temp_obj);

    SYN_LwM2M_TaskConfig cfg = {
        .client = &g_client,
        .transport = transport,
        .on_reboot = on_reboot,
        .rx_buf = g_rx_scratch,
        .rx_buf_size = sizeof(g_rx_scratch),
        .tx_buf = g_tx_scratch,
        .tx_buf_size = sizeof(g_tx_scratch),
    };
    syn_lwm2m_task_init(&g_task, &cfg);
}

docs.title: 11. Micro XRCE-DDS Client (proto/syn_xrce_dds.h)
docs.text:
Zero-heap, deterministic client engine for Micro-ROS & eProsima Micro XRCE-DDS v1.2: - CDR Serialization: Standard Little-Endian CDR serializer/deserializer with strict alignment rules. - Entity Tree: Complete ROS 2 hierarchy (DomainParticipant, Topic, Publisher, Subscriber, DataWriter, DataReader). - Framing & Transports: XRCE submessage framing over any SYN_Transport (UART, UDP, CAN).

#include <syntropic/proto/syn_xrce_dds.h>

static SYN_XRCE_Client g_xrce_client;
static uint8_t g_xrce_rx[256];
static uint8_t g_xrce_tx[256];

void xrce_setup(SYN_Transport *transport) {
    SYN_XRCE_Config cfg = {
        .transport = transport,
        .client_key = 0xCAFEBABEU,
        .session_id = 0x81U,
        .rx_buf = g_xrce_rx,
        .rx_buf_size = sizeof(g_xrce_rx),
        .tx_buf = g_xrce_tx,
        .tx_buf_size = sizeof(g_xrce_tx),
    };
    syn_xrce_client_init(&g_xrce_client, &cfg);
    syn_xrce_client_create_session(&g_xrce_client);
    syn_xrce_client_create_participant(&g_xrce_client, 1U);
    syn_xrce_client_create_topic(&g_xrce_client, 2U, 1U, "rt/chatter", "std_msgs::msg::dds_::String_");
    syn_xrce_client_create_publisher(&g_xrce_client, 3U, 1U);
    syn_xrce_client_create_datawriter(&g_xrce_client, 4U, 3U, 2U);
}

docs.title: 12. Micro OPC UA Embedded Server (proto/syn_opcua.h)
docs.text:
Zero-heap, deterministic IEC 62541 OPC UA binary server: - Protocol Framing: UACP (HEL/ACK/ERR) and UASC (OPN/CLO/MSG) framing. - Core Services: Read, Write, Browse, CreateSession, ActivateSession, CloseSession. - Address Space: Static in-memory address space with Object and Variable nodes, custom DataValue callbacks.

#include <syntropic/proto/syn_opcua.h>

static SYN_OPCUA_Server g_opcua_srv;
static uint8_t g_opcua_rx[512];
static uint8_t g_opcua_tx[512];

void opcua_setup(SYN_Transport *transport) {
    SYN_OPCUA_Config cfg = {
        .transport = transport,
        .endpoint_url = "opc.tcp://0.0.0.0:4840",
        .server_name = "SyntropicOS Edge Server",
        .rx_buf = g_opcua_rx,
        .rx_buf_size = sizeof(g_opcua_rx),
        .tx_buf = g_opcua_tx,
        .tx_buf_size = sizeof(g_opcua_tx),
    };
    syn_opcua_server_init(&g_opcua_srv, &cfg);

    SYN_OPCUA_Node var_node = {
        .node_id = {.ns_index = 1U, .id_type = SYN_OPCUA_NODEID_NUMERIC, .id = {.num = 1001U}},
        .browse_name = "SensorTemperature",
        .display_name = "SensorTemperature",
        .node_class = SYN_OPCUA_NODECLASS_VARIABLE,
        .data_type = SYN_OPCUA_TYPE_FLOAT,
        .value = {.value = {.type = SYN_OPCUA_TYPE_FLOAT, .val = {.float_val = 23.5f}},
