docs.title: 13. IO-Link Master & Device Protocol Engine (proto/syn_iolink.h)
docs.text:
Zero-heap IEC 61131-9 point-to-point digital protocol engine: - Physical Rates: COM1 (4.8k), COM2 (38.4k), COM3 (230.4k) baud. - Framing & Checksum: Standard 6-bit CRC with parity for M-Sequence Types 0, 1_1, 1_2, 2_1, 2_2, 2_V. - ISDU & Process Data: Cyclic process data exchange and acyclic Direct Parameter Page 1 and ISDU parameter read/write.

#include <syntropic/proto/syn_iolink.h>

static SYN_IOLink_Master g_iolink_master;
static uint8_t g_iolink_rx[128];
static uint8_t g_iolink_tx[128];

void iolink_setup(SYN_Transport *transport) {
    SYN_IOLink_MasterConfig cfg = {
        .transport = transport,
        .cycle_time_ms = 5U,
        .rx_buf = g_iolink_rx,
        .rx_buf_size = sizeof(g_iolink_rx),
        .tx_buf = g_iolink_tx,
        .tx_buf_size = sizeof(g_iolink_tx),
    };
    syn_iolink_master_init(&g_iolink_master, &cfg);
    syn_iolink_master_start(&g_iolink_master);
}

docs.title: 14. MQTT-SN Protocol Client Engine (proto/syn_mqttsn.h)
docs.text:
Zero-heap MQTT for Sensor Networks (MQTT-SN v1.2) client engine for constrained datagram transports (UDP, Zigbee, Thread, BLE, Sub-GHz): - Framing: 1-byte and 3-byte variable header lengths (payloads up to 64 KB). - Gateway Discovery: SEARCHGW, GWINFO, ADVERTISE. - Topic Addressing: Normal registered topics (16-bit IDs via REGISTER/REGACK), Predefined topic IDs, and Short 2-character topic IDs without registration handshake. - QoS Support: QoS 0, QoS 1 (with msg_id ack), and transparent QoS -1 (fire-and-forget without connect). - Power Optimization: Low-power SLEEP state and AWAKE ping flush. - Protothread Integration: syn_mqttsn_client_pt() coroutine for non-blocking task loops.

#include <syntropic/proto/syn_mqttsn.h>

static SYN_MQTTSN_Client g_sn_client;
static uint8_t g_sn_rx[256], g_sn_tx[256];

void on_sn_message(SYN_MQTTSN_Client *client, uint16_t topic_id, uint8_t topic_type,
                   const uint8_t *payload, size_t len, void *user_data) {
    (void)client;
    (void)topic_id;
    (void)topic_type;
    (void)payload;
    (void)len;
    (void)user_data;
    /* Process incoming sensor command */
}

void mqttsn_setup(SYN_Transport *datagram_transport) {
    SYN_MQTTSN_Config cfg = {
        .transport = datagram_transport,
        .client_id = "sensor_node_01",
        .duration_s = 60U,
        .clean_session = true,
        .on_message = on_sn_message,
        .rx_buf = g_sn_rx,
        .rx_buf_size = sizeof(g_sn_rx),
        .tx_buf = g_sn_tx,
        .tx_buf_size = sizeof(g_sn_tx),
    };
    syn_mqttsn_client_init(&g_sn_client, &cfg);
    syn_mqttsn_client_searchgw(&g_sn_client, 1U);
}

void publish_telemetry(int16_t temperature_c) {
    /* Publish to short 2-char topic 'te' at QoS 0 */
    syn_mqttsn_client_publish_short(&g_sn_client, "te", 0, false, (const uint8_t *)&temperature_c, sizeof(temperature_c));
}

docs.title: Control & Motor Modules
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides integer-only control algorithms, closed-loop PID controllers, trapezoidal motion profiling, and Field-Oriented Control (FOC) for BLDC/PMSM motors.

docs.title: Technical Specifications
docs.text: Feature Specification Math Format Fixed-point Q16.16 (q16_t) or normalized integer scaling. FPU Requirement None. Runs on ARM Cortex-M0/M3/M4, RISC-V, and 8-bit MCUs. Safety Features Anti-windup clamping, derivative filtering, stall detection, & limit events.

docs.title: 1. Closed-Loop PID Controller (control/syn_pid.h)
docs.text: The syn_pid module provides an integer-only PID controller with anti-windup clamping and derivative-term filtering.

docs.title: Control Loop Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Setpoint["Target Setpoint"] --> ErrorCalc["Error = Setpoint - Feedback"]
    Feedback --> ErrorCalc
    ErrorCalc --> PID["SYN_PID (Kp, Ki, Kd)"]
    PID --> AntiWindup["Anti-Windup Clamp (Min/Max Out)"]
    AntiWindup --> Actuator["PWM / Motor Drive Output"]

docs.title: Complete Code Example (Integer PID Temperature / Speed Control)
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/control/syn_pid.h>

static SYN_PID pid;

void control_init(void) {
    // Configure PID gains: kp = 2.5, ki = 0.5/s, kd = 0.1, scale = 256, Output: 0..1000
    SYN_PID_Config cfg = SYN_PID_GAINS(2.5, 0.5, 0.1, 256, 0, 1000);
    cfg.integral_max = 500;
    syn_pid_init(&pid, &cfg);
}

uint16_t control_step(int32_t setpoint, int32_t current_reading, uint32_t dt_ms) {
    // Compute control output step
    int32_t output = syn_pid_update(&pid, setpoint, current_reading, dt_ms);
    return (uint16_t)output;
}

docs.title: 2. Stepper Motor Control (motor/syn_stepper.h)
docs.text:
Provides Step/Direction motor driving with trapezoidal velocity acceleration profiles.

#include <syntropic/motor/syn_stepper.h>

static SYN_Stepper stepper;

void stepper_init(void) {
    // Initialize pin 4 (step), pin 5 (dir), max_speed = 1000 steps/s, accel = 500 steps/s²
    syn_stepper_init(&stepper, 4, 5);
    syn_stepper_set_speed(&stepper, 1000, 500);
}

void move_relative(int32_t steps) {
    syn_stepper_move(&stepper, steps);
}

void main_timer_isr(void) {
    // Serves step generation (call at fixed interrupt interval e.g. 10 kHz)
    syn_stepper_tick(&stepper);
}

docs.title: 3. Field-Oriented Control (FOC) (motor/syn_foc.h)
docs.text:
Provides Clarke/Park transforms, Space Vector PWM (SVPWM), and Sliding Mode Observers (SMO) for sensorless BLDC/PMSM motor control in pure Q16.16 fixed-point math.

#include <syntropic/motor/syn_foc.h>
#include <syntropic/motor/syn_foc_observer.h>

static SYN_FOCObserver observer;

void foc_setup(void) {
    SYN_FOCObserverConfig cfg = {
        .R = Q16_FROM_FLOAT(0.5f),    // 0.5 Ohm phase resistance
        .L = Q16_FROM_FLOAT(0.001f),  // 1 mH phase inductance
        .G = Q16_FROM_INT(10),        // Sliding mode observer gain
        .dt = Q16_FROM_FLOAT(0.0001f),// 10 kHz sampling period (100 µs)
        .Kp_pll = Q16_FROM_INT(150),
        .Ki_pll = Q16_FROM_INT(6000)
    };
    syn_foc_observer_init(&observer, &cfg);
}

void foc_10khz_isr(q16_t v_alpha, q16_t v_beta, q16_t i_alpha, q16_t i_beta) {
    // 1. Update Sliding Mode Observer with phase voltages and currents
    syn_foc_observer_update(&observer, v_alpha, v_beta, i_alpha, i_beta);

    // 2. Read estimated rotor angle theta_e [0, 2pi) and speed omega_e
    q16_t est_angle = syn_foc_observer_get_angle(&observer);
    q16_t est_speed = syn_foc_observer_get_speed(&observer);
}

docs.title: 4. G-Code & NIST RS-274 Motion Interpreter (motor/syn_gcode.h)
docs.text:
Zero-heap streaming ASCII G-code parser and multi-axis trajectory coordinator: - Parser: Streaming word extraction (G, M, X, Y, Z, I, J, K, F, S, P, T). - Modal Engine: G0/G1/G2/G3/G4, G17/G18/G19 planes, G20/G21 units, G90/G91 distance modes, G92 offsets, M3/M4/M5 spindle control, M7/M8/M9 coolant. - Interpolator Integration: Automatic trajectory planning via SYN_Interpolator with S-curve/trapezoidal velocity profiles.

#include <syntropic/motor/syn_gcode.h>
#include <syntropic/motor/syn_interpolator.h>

static SYN_Interpolator g_interp;
static SYN_GCode_Controller g_gcode_ctrl;

void gcode_setup(void) {
    SYN_GCode_Config cfg = {
        .interpolator = &g_interp,
        .default_feedrate = 200.0f,
        .max_acceleration = 1000.0f,
        .max_jerk = 5000.0f,
        .step_resolution = 0.001f,
    };
    syn_gcode_init(&g_gcode_ctrl, &cfg);

    /* Stream G-code blocks */
    syn_gcode_execute_line(&g_gcode_ctrl, "G21 G90 G0 X0 Y0 Z5");
    syn_gcode_execute_line(&g_gcode_ctrl, "G1 Z-1 F100");
    syn_gcode_execute_line(&g_gcode_ctrl, "G2 X10 Y10 I5 J0 F300");
}

docs.title: 5. Multi-Axis Robot Kinematics (motor/syn_kinematics.h)
docs.text:
Zero-heap integer Q16.16 multi-axis robot kinematics engine: - Transforms & Conventions: Standard and Modified Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) 4x4 matrix transforms. - Forward Kinematics: Arbitrary N-DOF serial manipulator forward kinematics with 3D position and roll/pitch/yaw Euler orientations. - Differential Kinematics: Exact 6xN Geometric Jacobian computation for velocity mapping and singularity analysis. - Standard Robot Models: - 3-DOF Planar Articulated Arm (FK & analytical IK with Elbow-Up / Elbow-Down selection). - 4-DOF SCARA Robot (FK & analytical IK with tool pitch/yaw). - 6-DOF PUMA Manipulator with Spherical Wrist (FK & Pieper analytical decoupling IK). - 3-Axis Delta Parallel Robot (FK via 3-sphere intersection & analytical IK).

#include <syntropic/motor/syn_kinematics.h>

void scara_pick_and_place_demo(void) {
    SYN_Kinematics_SCARAConfig cfg = {
        .l1 = Q16_FROM_INT(200),     /* 200 mm inner arm */
        .l2 = Q16_FROM_INT(150),     /* 150 mm outer arm */
        .d_max = Q16_FROM_INT(100),  /* 100 mm Z stroke */
        .z_home = Q16_FROM_INT(100), /* 100 mm home height */
    };

    /* Define target 6D pose */
    SYN_Pose6D target = {
        .position = {.x = Q16_FROM_INT(250), .y = Q16_FROM_INT(100), .z = Q16_FROM_INT(20)},
        .orientation = {.roll = 0, .pitch = 0, .yaw = Q16_PI / 4}
    };

    q16_t q1 = 0, q2 = 0, d3 = 0, q4 = 0;
    if (syn_kinematics_scara_ik(&cfg, &target, SYN_ARM_ELBOW_UP, &q1, &q2, &d3, &q4) == SYN_OK) {
        /* Drive joint actuators to solved angles */
    }
}

docs.title: 6. Additional Motor Drivers, Closed-Loop Controllers & Flight / RC Control
Motor Drivers & Closed-Loop Servo/Actuator Stack (motor/*.h)
docs.text:
• Motor Hardware Abstraction (motor/syn_motor_output.h, header-only): Three-callback vtable (SYN_MotorOutput: set_output, coast, brake) decoupling closed-loop controllers from PWM/H-bridge drivers.
  • H-Bridge DC Motor (motor/syn_dc_motor.h, SYN_USE_DC_MOTOR): Drives PWM+Dir or Dual-PWM H-bridges (SYN_DCMotor: syn_dc_motor_init, syn_dc_motor_set_speed, syn_dc_motor_ramp_to, syn_dc_motor_coast, syn_dc_motor_brake, syn_dc_motor_output).
  • Hobby Servo (motor/syn_servo.h, SYN_USE_SERVO): Maps degree targets or raw microsecond commands onto pulse_min..pulse_max (SYN_Servo: syn_servo_init, syn_servo_set_angle, syn_servo_move_to, syn_servo_update).
  • 6-Step Trapezoidal BLDC (motor/syn_bldc_6step.h, SYN_USE_BLDC_6STEP): Commutates 3-phase bridges from 3-bit Hall states (SYN_BLDC_6Step: syn_bldc_6step_init, syn_bldc_6step_set_hall, syn_bldc_6step_update_speed) with invalid-Hall fault detection and closed-loop RPM PID.
  • FOC Rotor Encoder Interface (motor/syn_foc_encoder.h): Converts ABZ quadrature counts, 3-phase Hall transitions, or 14-bit absolute angles into Q16.16 electrical angle and speed (syn_foc_encoder_init, syn_foc_encoder_get_elec_angle, syn_foc_encoder_get_elec_speed).
  • Closed-Loop Motor Controller (motor/syn_motor_ctrl.h, SYN_USE_MOTOR_CTRL): Combines SYN_MotorOutput + position reader with PID, velocity/acceleration feedforward (ff_kv, ff_ka), trapezoidal and S-curve moves (syn_motor_ctrl_move_to, syn_motor_ctrl_move_to_scurve), soft travel limits, and stall detection.
  • Linear Actuator (motor/syn_actuator.h, SYN_USE_ACTUATOR): Closed-loop stroke positioner (0..1000 = 0.0%..100.0%) over potentiometer ADC feedback (syn_actuator_init, syn_actuator_set_position, syn_actuator_update).
  • Multi-Axis Trajectory Interpolator (motor/syn_interpolator.h, SYN_USE_INTERPOLATOR): Coordinated 2D/3D linear, XY/ZX/YZ helical circular arc, and cubic Bezier S-curve motion planner (syn_interpolator_plan_linear, syn_interpolator_plan_circular, syn_interpolator_plan_circular_plane, syn_interpolator_plan_bezier, syn_interpolator_step).

docs.title: Auto-Tuning, Loop Diagnostics & Flight / RC Control (control/*.h)
docs.text:
• Relay & Feedforward Auto-Tuner (control/syn_autotune.h, SYN_USE_AUTOTUNE): Identifies ff_kv/ff_ka and Ziegler-Nichols or Tyreus-Luyben PID gains on SYN_MotorCtrl within bounded travel/watchdog limits (syn_autotune_init, syn_autotune_start, syn_autotune_update, syn_autotune_apply).
  • Control Loop Statistics (control/syn_control_stats.h): Tracks RMS error, peak error, RMS effort, output slew jitter, and ITAE (syn_control_stats_update, syn_control_stats_report).
  • Cascaded 3-Axis Flight PID & Quad-X Mixer (control/syn_flight_pid.h, SYN_USE_FLIGHT_PID): Outer-angle + inner-rate Q16.16 roll/pitch/yaw loops mixing into 4 motor 1000..2000 us outputs (syn_flight_init, syn_flight_update).
  • RC Stick Curve & Link Failsafe (control/syn_rc_curve.h, SYN_USE_RC_CURVE; control/syn_rc_failsafe.h, SYN_USE_RC_FAILSAFE): Applies deadband, cubic expo, and dual-rate scaling (syn_rc_curve_apply) and enforces per-channel hold/preset/disarm actions on receiver timeout (syn_failsafe_init, syn_failsafe_feed_frame, syn_failsafe_step).

docs.title: Core & Utility Modules
docs.text: src/syntropic/common/ and src/syntropic/util/ provide SyntropicOS's zero-heap foundation: status codes, compiler portability macros, lock-free ISR-to-task queues, static block/slab allocators, wire codecs (JSON, CBOR, Protobuf, Base64, LZ4, CRC), string formatting, finite state machines, pub/sub messaging, Q16.16 fixed-point linear algebra, motion profiles, and timing helpers.

docs.title: 1. Foundation, Compiler, Bits & Asserts
docs.text:
• common/syn_defs.h (always enabled): Core return enum SYN_Status (SYN_OK = 0, SYN_ERROR, SYN_BUSY, SYN_TIMEOUT, SYN_INVALID_PARAM, SYN_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, SYN_NOT_FOUND), SYN_GPIO_Pin, SYN_GPIO_Mode, SYN_UARTInstance, and utility macros (SYN_ARRAY_SIZE, SYN_UNUSED_VAR, SYN_MIN, SYN_MAX, SYN_ABS, SYN_SIGN, SYN_CLAMP).
  • common/syn_compiler.h (always enabled): Portable toolchain attributes across GCC, Clang, ARM Compiler, and IAR (SYN_WEAK, SYN_PACKED, SYN_INLINE, SYN_UNUSED, SYN_NORETURN, SYN_STATIC_ASSERT(expr, msg), SYN_SECTION(name), SYN_ALIGN(n), SYN_COMPILER_BARRIER(), SYN_FALLTHROUGH).
  • common/syn_barrier.h (always enabled; hardware fence when SYN_USE_MULTICORE=1): SYN_LOAD_ACQUIRE(ptr) / SYN_STORE_RELEASE(ptr, val) (syn_load_acquire, syn_store_release) memory-ordering primitives for ISR and dual-core lock-free structures.
  • util/syn_bits.h (header-only): Bit/field manipulation macros (SYN_BIT, SYN_BIT_SET, SYN_BIT_CLEAR, SYN_BIT_TOGGLE, SYN_BIT_CHECK, SYN_BITMASK(width, offset), SYN_BITS_GET, SYN_BITS_SET, SYN_BITS_TO_BYTES).
  • util/syn_assert.h (header-only): SYN_ASSERT(expr) invokes weak syn_assert_failed(const char *file, int line) on violation; define SYN_DISABLE_ASSERT in syn_config.h to compile all asserts to ((void)0).

docs.title: Cooperative Byte Stream (util/syn_stream.h)
docs.text:
SYN_Stream wraps a lock-free SYN_RingBuf with protothread wake conditions (PT_STREAM_WAIT polled or PT_BLOCK_STREAM scheduler-parked): - Default mode: Readable when >= 1 byte is buffered. - Threshold mode (syn_stream_set_threshold(&s, n)): Readable when >= n bytes arrive. - Delimiter mode (syn_stream_set_delimiter(&s, '\n')): Readable when the delimiter byte arrives. If an oversized frame fills the buffer without a delimiter, SYN_Stream flushes the partial frame and discards trailing bytes until the next delimiter arrives so syn_stream_read_line() never returns a truncated frame.

#include "syntropic/syntropic.h"

static uint8_t s_raw_buf[128];
static SYN_Stream s_rx_stream;

void stream_setup(void) {
    syn_stream_init(&s_rx_stream, s_raw_buf, sizeof(s_raw_buf));
    syn_stream_set_delimiter(&s_rx_stream, '\n');
}

/* ISR producer: lock-free single-byte push */
void uart_rx_isr_byte(uint8_t byte) {
    (void)syn_stream_put(&s_rx_stream, byte);
}

/* Protothread consumer: wakes on complete '\n'-terminated lines */
SYN_PT_Status line_consumer_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task) {
    static uint8_t line_buf[64];
    size_t len;
    (void)task;

    PT_BEGIN(pt);
    for (;;) {
        PT_STREAM_WAIT(pt, &s_rx_stream);
        len = syn_stream_read_line(&s_rx_stream, line_buf, sizeof(line_buf));
        (void)len;
    }
    PT_END(pt);
}

docs.title: Byte Ring Buffer, Typed SPSC Queue & Ping-Pong Buffer
docs.text:
• util/syn_ringbuf.h (SYN_RingBuf, always enabled): Lock-free SPSC byte ring buffer (size - 1 usable capacity) with single-byte (syn_ringbuf_put, syn_ringbuf_get, syn_ringbuf_peek) and bulk (syn_ringbuf_write, syn_ringbuf_read, syn_ringbuf_peek_n) APIs.
  • util/syn_spsc_queue.h (SYN_SPSC_Queue, always enabled): Lock-free SPSC queue for fixed-size structs (syn_spsc_queue_init(&q, buf, sizeof(elem), cap), syn_spsc_queue_push, syn_spsc_queue_pop, PT_QUEUE_WAIT_POP, PT_BLOCK_QUEUE_POP).
  • util/syn_pingpong.h (SYN_PingPong, header-only): Zero-copy double buffer for DMA/ISR producers (syn_pingpong_init(&pp, buf_a, buf_b, sz), syn_pingpong_active for ISR writes, syn_pingpong_swap on completion, syn_pingpong_ready / syn_pingpong_ready_buf / syn_pingpong_consume in task context).

docs.title: 3. Static Memory Allocators (syn_pool & syn_slab)
docs.text:
SyntropicOS forbids malloc(), providing two deterministic O(1) static allocators backed by caller-owned byte arrays:

  • util/syn_pool.h (SYN_USE_POOL, header-only): Fixed-size block pool with embedded freelist, double-free detection bitmap, and syn_pool_high_watermark() tracking. Size backing storage with SYN_POOL_BUF_SIZE(block_size, count).
  • util/syn_slab.h (always enabled): Multi-class slab allocator (SYN_SlabAllocator, up to SYN_SLAB_MAX_CLASSES = 8 sorted block sizes) routing syn_slab_alloc(&slab, size) to the smallest fitting class in O(1) time without fragmentation.
#include "syntropic/util/syn_pool.h"

#define PKT_SIZE  64U
#define PKT_COUNT 8U

static uint8_t s_pool_mem[SYN_POOL_BUF_SIZE(PKT_SIZE, PKT_COUNT)];
static SYN_Pool s_pkt_pool;

void pkt_pool_setup(void) {
    syn_pool_init(&s_pkt_pool, s_pool_mem, sizeof(s_pool_mem), PKT_SIZE);
    void *blk = syn_pool_alloc(&s_pkt_pool);
    if (blk != NULL) {
        syn_pool_free(&s_pkt_pool, blk);
    }
}

docs.title: 4. Binary Packing, Checksums, Compression & Wire Codecs
Endian-Safe Packing & CRC (syn_pack.h, syn_crc.h)
docs.text:
• util/syn_pack.h (header-only): Alignment-safe wire serialization preventing unaligned-access faults on Cortex-M0/M0+:
  • Advancing cursor (size_t *pos): syn_pack_u8/u16/u32/u64, syn_pack_i8/i16/i32, syn_pack_bytes, syn_unpack_*, plus little-endian _le variants (syn_pack_u16_le, syn_unpack_u32_le, etc.).
  • Non-advancing offset (size_t pos): syn_peek_u8/u16/u32[_le] and syn_poke_u16/u32[_le].
  • util/syn_crc.h (always enabled; SYN_CRC_USE_TABLE = 1 table / 0 bitwise): Single-shot and streaming (_update) calculators for CRC-8/MAXIM (syn_crc8), CRC-16/CCITT (syn_crc16_ccitt), CRC-16/Modbus (syn_crc16_modbus), and CRC-32 (syn_crc32).

docs.title: Structured Codecs & Compression (JSON, CBOR, Protobuf, Base64, LZ4)
5. Strings & printf-Free Formatting (syn_str.h, syn_fmt.h)
docs.text:
• util/syn_str.h (always enabled): In-place delimiter splitting (syn_str_split), whitespace trimming (syn_str_trim), and overflow-checked integer parsing (syn_str_to_i32, syn_str_to_u32).
  • util/syn_fmt.h (SYN_USE_FMT): Formats numbers and buffers without pulling in C library snprintf: syn_fmt_int, syn_fmt_uint, syn_fmt_hex, syn_fmt_hex_parse, syn_fmt_q16, syn_fmt_fixed, syn_fmt_hexdump, and syn_fmt_concat.

docs.title: 6. State Machines, Events, Pub/Sub & Concurrency
docs.text:
• util/syn_fsm.h (SYN_USE_FSM): Table-driven SYN_FSM supporting SYN_FSM_Transition tables (from, event, to, SYN_FSM_Guard, SYN_FSM_Action), per-state entry/exit hooks (SYN_FSM_StateDesc), and syn_fsm_dispatch(). See Cross-Module Integration for pairing syn_fsm with syn_ao Active Objects.
  • util/syn_pubsub.h (SYN_USE_PUBSUB): Topic-addressed publish/subscribe broker (SYN_PubSubBroker) over a caller-owned SYN_PubSubSub array (syn_pubsub_init, syn_pubsub_subscribe, syn_pubsub_publish, wildcard SYN_PUBSUB_TOPIC_ALL).
  • util/syn_event.h (SYN_USE_EVENT) & util/syn_spinlock.h (SYN_USE_MULTICORE): 32-bit SYN_EventGroup (PT_WAIT_EVENT, PT_WAIT_EVENT_ANY) and scoped SYN_SPINLOCK_GUARD(id). Full synchronization details are covered in Cooperative Multitasking.

docs.title: 7. Fixed-Point Math, Linear Algebra, 3D Transforms & Geodesy
docs.text:
• util/syn_qmath.h (SYN_USE_QMATH): q16_t (Q16.16), q15_t (Q0.15), and q7_t (Q0.7) fixed-point types, saturating arithmetic (q16_add_sat, q16_sub_sat, q16_mul_sat), interpolation (q16_lerp), integer square roots (syn_isqrt32, syn_isqrt64), transcendentals (q16_sin, q16_cos, q16_sincos_fast, q16_atan2, q16_sqrt, q16_rsqrt, q16_exp, q16_log, q16_pow), and string conversion (q16_to_str, q16_from_str).
  • util/syn_vector.h (always enabled): Elementwise q16_t vector ops (syn_vec_add, syn_vec_sub, syn_vec_scale, syn_vec_clamp) and statistical reductions (syn_vec_min, syn_vec_max, syn_vec_mean, syn_vec_variance, syn_vec_rms).
  • util/syn_matrix.h (SYN_USE_MATRIX): Caller-backed SYN_Matrix (SYN_MAT_DECL, SYN_MAT_STATIC), 2D/3D homogeneous transforms, dot/cross products, and numerical solvers (syn_matrix_solve_lu, syn_matrix_solve_cholesky, syn_matrix_least_squares, syn_matrix_qr, syn_matrix_eigen_sym2/3).
  • util/syn_quaternion.h (always enabled): SYN_Quaternion 3D orientation math (syn_quat_mul, syn_quat_normalize, syn_quat_rotate_vec3, syn_quat_from_euler, syn_quat_to_euler, syn_quat_to_mat3x3, syn_quat_slerp).
  • util/syn_transform.h (always enabled): Q16.16 Cartesian <-> Polar (syn_cart2pol, syn_pol2cart) and Cartesian <-> Spherical (syn_cart2sph, syn_sph2cart) coordinate conversions.
  • util/syn_geo.h (SYN_USE_GEO): WGS-84 <-> ECEF <-> local ENU transformations (syn_geo_wgs84_to_enu), Haversine and fixed-point micro-degree distances (syn_geo_haversine_m, syn_geo_distance_fixed_mm), and NMEA GGA position extraction (syn_geo_pos_from_gga).
  • util/syn_lut.h (header-only): Piecewise-linear 1D lookup table (SYN_LUT_Entry) with clamped forward (syn_lut_forward) and inverse (syn_lut_reverse) interpolation.
  • util/syn_nn.h (always enabled): Quantized q7_t TinyML layers (Dense, Conv1D, Attention, Pooling, Softmax, syn_nn_dense_pt / syn_nn_conv1d_pt). Covered in DSP & Filters.

docs.title: 8. Motion Profiles & Signal Conditioning
docs.text:
• util/syn_ramp.h (SYN_USE_RAMP): Linear slew-rate (syn_ramp_set_target) and trapezoidal velocity/acceleration (syn_ramp_set_target_trapezoid, syn_ramp_set_target_trapezoid_fp) setpoint generators updated per tick via syn_ramp_update().
  • util/syn_scurve.h (SYN_USE_SCURVE): 7-phase jerk-limited 1D (SYN_SCurve) and coordinated 3-axis (SYN_SCurve3D, syn_scurve3d_plan / syn_scurve3d_update) trajectory generator bounding v_max, a_max, and j_max.
  • util/syn_hysteresis.h (header-only): Schmitt-trigger integer comparator (SYN_Hysteresis, syn_hyst_init, syn_hyst_update) switching at threshold +/- band to suppress relay/alarm chatter.
  • util/syn_change_filter.h (header-only): Report-on-change gate (SYN_ChangeFilter, syn_change_filter_update) requiring both |delta| >= dead_band and elapsed time >= min_interval_ms.

docs.title: 9. Timing, Retry Backoff, Rate Limiting, PRNG & Metrics
docs.text:
• util/syn_timeout.h (header-only): 32-bit wrap-safe deadline tracker (SYN_Timeout: syn_timeout_start, syn_timeout_expired, syn_timeout_remaining, drift-free syn_timeout_periodic, and PT_WAIT_TIMEOUT(pt, &to)).
  • util/syn_backoff.h (always enabled): Exponential retry backoff (SYN_Backoff: syn_backoff_init, syn_backoff_next_ms, syn_backoff_exhausted, syn_backoff_reset) with 1.0x–1.5x random jitter.
  • util/syn_rate_limit.h (header-only): Token-bucket rate limiter (SYN_RateLimit: syn_rate_limit_init(&rl, max_tokens, interval_ms), syn_rate_limit_allow).
  • util/syn_random.h (always enabled): syn_random_fill, syn_random_u32, and syn_random_range(min, max) delegating to platform syn_port_random_fill() (overrideable weak hook with xorshift test fallback).
  • util/syn_metrics.h (SYN_USE_METRICS, opt-in default 0): Intrusive static counter/gauge registry (SYN_METRIC_DECLARE, SYN_METRIC_REGISTER, SYN_METRIC_INC/ADD/SET, syn_metrics_foreach); compiles to zero-cost no-ops when SYN_USE_METRICS is 0.

docs.title: Cryptography & Security Modules
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides pure C99, constant-time cryptographic primitives and AEAD ciphers designed for resource-constrained microcontrollers.

docs.title: Technical Specifications
docs.text: Feature Specification Constant-Time Branchless arithmetic operations to prevent side-channel timing attacks. Memory Allocation 100% Zero-Heap. All operations use caller-owned stacks or buffers. Standards Compliance BLAKE2s (RFC 7693), ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439), X25519 (RFC 7748).

docs.title: 1. BLAKE2s Cryptographic Hash (crypto/syn_blake2s.h)
docs.text:
BLAKE2s-256 provides high-speed cryptographic hashing and keyed-MAC authentication (HMAC replacement without HMAC overhead).

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_blake2s.h>

void hash_payload(const uint8_t *msg, size_t len, uint8_t digest[32]) {
    // One-shot BLAKE2s-256 hash
    syn_blake2s(msg, len, digest, 32);
}

void compute_mac(const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len, const uint8_t *msg, size_t msg_len, uint8_t tag[16]) {
    SYN_BLAKE2s ctx;
    syn_blake2s_init_keyed(&ctx, key, key_len, 16);
    syn_blake2s_update(&ctx, msg, msg_len);
    syn_blake2s_final(&ctx, tag);
}

docs.title: 2. ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD Cipher (crypto/syn_chacha20poly1305.h)
docs.text:
Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) per RFC 8439.

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_chacha20poly1305.h>

void encrypt_sensor_telemetry(void) {
    uint8_t key[32] = { /* 256-bit symmetric key */ };
    uint8_t nonce[12] = { /* 96-bit unique nonce */ };

    uint8_t payload[64] = "Temperature=24.5C;Humidity=60%";
    uint8_t ciphertext[64];
    uint8_t auth_tag[16];

    // Encrypt and authenticate payload
    syn_aead_encrypt(key, nonce,
                     NULL, 0, // Additional Authenticated Data (AAD)
                     payload, sizeof(payload),
                     ciphertext, auth_tag);
}

docs.title: 3. X25519 ECDH Key Exchange (crypto/syn_x25519.h)
docs.text:
Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (Curve25519 / RFC 7748) key exchange for secure peer-to-peer session key negotiation.

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_x25519.h>

void ecdh_key_exchange(const uint8_t peer_public[32], uint8_t my_public[32],
                       uint8_t shared_secret[32]) {
    uint8_t my_private[32] = { /* 32 CSPRNG bytes */ };

    // Clamp private scalar per RFC 7748 and derive public key: P = k * G
    syn_x25519_clamp(my_private);
    syn_x25519_pubkey(my_public, my_private);

    // Derive shared secret: S = k * Peer_P
    syn_x25519(shared_secret, my_private, peer_public);
}

docs.title: 4. SHA-256 Hash Engine (crypto/syn_sha256.h)
docs.text:
Standard NIST FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 digest computation for bootloader firmware verification and packet checksums.

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_sha256.h>

void sha256_demo(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, uint8_t hash[32]) {
    syn_sha256(data, len, hash);
}

docs.title: 5. NIST P-256 (secp256r1) Elliptic Curve Engine (crypto/syn_p256.h)
docs.text:
Full cleanroom implementation of NIST P-256 ECC arithmetic in Jacobian projective coordinates featuring: - Solinas Fast Modular Reduction ($p = 2^{256} - 2^{224} + 2^{192} + 2^{96} - 1$ per FIPS 186-4 §D.2.1). - Constant-Time Scalar Multiplication (point_cmov 4-bit fixed windowing) with zero side-channel branching. - ECDH Key Agreement (RFC 5903). - ECDSA Sign & Verify (RFC 6979 / ANSI X9.62).

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_p256.h>

void p256_ecdh_and_ecdsa_demo(void) {
    uint8_t priv_key[32] = { /* 256-bit scalar */ };
    uint8_t pub_x[32], pub_y[32];

    // Derive public key: Q = d * G
    syn_p256_base_mul(priv_key, pub_x, pub_y);

    // Compute shared ECDH secret: S = d * Peer_Q
    uint8_t peer_x[32], peer_y[32], shared_secret[32];
    syn_p256_ecdh(priv_key, peer_x, peer_y, shared_secret);

    // Sign SHA-256 digest with ECDSA
    uint8_t hash[32], nonce_k[32], r[32], s[32];
    syn_p256_sign_ecdsa(priv_key, nonce_k, hash, r, s);

    // Verify ECDSA signature
    bool valid = syn_p256_verify_ecdsa(hash, r, s, pub_x, pub_y);
}

docs.title: 6. TCG TPM 2.0 Command Marshaller & Measured Boot Engine (crypto/syn_tpm2.h)
docs.text:
Complete cleanroom TCG TPM 2.0 serializer and response parser for hardware security chips (SPI / I2C TPM): - Core Operations: TPM2_Startup, TPM2_SelfTest, TPM2_GetRandom. - Platform Configuration Registers (PCRs): TPM2_PCR_Read and TPM2_PCR_Extend (SHA-256, SHA-384) for measured boot integrity chains. - Remote Attestation: TPM2_Quote over selected PCR banks with nonce verification. - Hardware NVRAM: Authenticated TPM2_NV_Read and TPM2_NV_Write.

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_tpm2.h>

static SYN_TPM2_Context g_tpm;
static uint8_t g_tpm_rx[512], g_tpm_tx[512];

void tpm2_setup(SYN_Transport *tpm_spi_transport) {
    SYN_TPM2_Config cfg = {
        .transport = tpm_spi_transport,
        .rx_buf = g_tpm_rx,
        .rx_buf_size = sizeof(g_tpm_rx),
        .tx_buf = g_tpm_tx,
        .tx_buf_size = sizeof(g_tpm_tx),
    };
    syn_tpm2_init(&g_tpm, &cfg);
    syn_tpm2_startup(&g_tpm, SYN_TPM2_SU_CLEAR);
}

void measure_stage2_firmware(const uint8_t *fw_sha256) {
    /* Extend PCR 0 with bootloader / kernel measurement */
    syn_tpm2_pcr_extend(&g_tpm, 0U, SYN_TPM2_ALG_SHA256, fw_sha256, 32U);
}

docs.title: 7. AES Block/AEAD Modes, SHA-512, HMAC/HKDF, DRBG, Ed25519 & X.509 PKI
docs.text: Module Guard Primary API Summary crypto/syn_aes.h SYN_USE_AES syn_aes_init, syn_aes_cbc_encrypt/decrypt, syn_aes_ctr, syn_aes_gcm_encrypt/decrypt, syn_aes_ccm_encrypt/decrypt Constant-time AES-128/192/256 ECB, PKCS#7 CBC, CTR, AES-GCM AEAD, and AES-CCM AEAD via bitsliced Boyar–Peralta circuit on non-AVR (AVR retains single-cycle PROGMEM tables); optional SYN_USE_PORT_AES hardware offload crypto/syn_aes_cmac.h SYN_USE_AES_CMAC syn_aes_cmac, syn_aes_cmac_verify Constant-time 128-bit AES-CMAC (RFC 4493 / NIST SP 800-38B) crypto/syn_hmac.h SYN_USE_SHA256 syn_hmac_sha256_init/update/final, syn_hmac_sha256 Streaming and single-shot HMAC-SHA256 with stack state zeroization crypto/syn_sha512.h SYN_USE_SHA512 syn_sha512, syn_sha384, syn_hmac_sha512, syn_hmac_sha384 FIPS 180-4 SHA-512 / SHA-384 digests and RFC 4231 HMACs crypto/syn_hkdf.h SYN_USE_HKDF syn_hkdf_extract, syn_hkdf_expand, syn_hkdf, syn_hkdf_expand_label RFC 5869 HKDF and RFC 8446 TLS 1.3 HKDF-Expand-Label (SHA-256/384/512) crypto/syn_hmac_drbg.h SYN_USE_HMAC_DRBG syn_hmac_drbg_init, syn_hmac_drbg_reseed, syn_hmac_drbg_generate NIST SP 800-90A Rev. 1 HMAC-DRBG (SHA-256) CSPRNG crypto/syn_ed25519.h SYN_USE_ED25519 syn_ed25519_create_keypair, syn_ed25519_sign, syn_ed25519_verify RFC 8032 Ed25519 deterministic digital signatures crypto/syn_asn1.h SYN_USE_ASN1 syn_asn1_parse_element, syn_asn1_step, syn_asn1_enter_container, syn_asn1_match_oid Zero-copy ASN.1 DER TLV container, OID, integer, and bit-string parser crypto/syn_x509.h SYN_USE_X509 syn_x509_parse, syn_x509_verify_signature, syn_x509_validate_chain DER X.509 v3 certificate parser and Ed25519 / ECDSA-P256 chain validator

docs.title: 8. Cooperative Protothread Crypto API (*_init / *_pt / *_wipe)
docs.text:
Asymmetric scalar multiplication, signing, and certificate verification expose caller-owned, zero-heap contexts that run as SYN_PT child protothreads. Each slice executes bounded field, ladder, or hash steps and yields PT_MORE until returning PT_ENDED.

Module Context Initializers Child Protothreads Cancellation Wipe crypto/syn_x25519.h SYN_X25519_Ctx syn_x25519_init, syn_x25519_pubkey_init syn_x25519_pt syn_x25519_wipe crypto/syn_p256.h SYN_P256_Ctx syn_p256_base_mul_init, syn_p256_point_mul_init, syn_p256_sign_init, syn_p256_sign_deterministic_init, syn_p256_verify_init syn_p256_mul_pt, syn_p256_sign_pt, syn_p256_verify_pt syn_p256_wipe crypto/syn_ed25519.h SYN_Ed25519_Ctx syn_ed25519_publickey_init, syn_ed25519_sign_init, syn_ed25519_verify_init, syn_ed25519_verify_hash_init syn_ed25519_publickey_pt, syn_ed25519_sign_pt, syn_ed25519_verify_pt syn_ed25519_wipe crypto/syn_x509.h SYN_X509_VerifyCtx syn_x509_verify_signature_init, syn_x509_validate_chain_init syn_x509_verify_pt syn_x509_verify_wipe

Compose child protothreads inside scheduler tasks with PT_SPAWN_IF_NEEDED (sched/syn_sched.h). Uncontended dispatches run consecutive PT_MORE slices in one turn; contended dispatches (syn_task_should_share(task)) yield PT_MORE between slices:

#include <syntropic/crypto/syn_x25519.h>
#include <syntropic/sched/syn_sched.h>

typedef struct {
    SYN_PT child_pt;
    SYN_X25519_Ctx x25519;
    uint8_t priv[32];
    uint8_t peer_pub[32];
    uint8_t shared[32];
} KeyExState;

SYN_PT_Status key_exchange_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task)
{
    KeyExState *st = (KeyExState *)task->user_data;

    PT_BEGIN(pt);

    if (!syn_x25519_init(&st->x25519, st->priv, st->peer_pub)) {
        PT_EXIT(pt);
    }
    PT_SPAWN_IF_NEEDED(pt, task, &st->child_pt,
                       syn_x25519_pt(&st->child_pt, &st->x25519, st->shared));

    PT_END(pt);
}

Zeroization & Cancellation Cleanup: Every *_pt function scrubs its working context via volatile syn_secure_zero before returning PT_ENDED. If a caller aborts, times out, or resets a task before PT_ENDED, call the matching *_wipe function (syn_x25519_wipe, syn_p256_wipe, syn_ed25519_wipe, syn_x509_verify_wipe) so syn_secure_zero clears clamped scalars, nonces, and intermediate field state.

docs.title: Debug & Diagnostic Modules
docs.text: SyntropicOS includes lightweight, zero-overhead diagnostic tools designed specifically for constrained embedded systems. They operate without dynamic memory allocations (malloc), long string formatting overhead, or blocking UART prints.

docs.title: 1. Lightweight Event Tracer (syn_trace.h)
docs.text: The syn_trace module is a high-speed, timestamped circular event recorder. It allows ISRs and tasks to record events in real-time with millisecond timestamps (syn_port_get_tick_ms()) without string-formatting overhead.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fixed-size caller-owned circular buffer (SYN_TraceEntry).
  • Safe to record inside Interrupt Service Routines (ISRs).
  • Zero string formatting during record time.
  • Post-mortem dump over Serial CLI or GDB debugger.

docs.title: Architecture Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    ISR["Hardware ISR"] -->|SYN_TRACE| RingBuffer["SYN_Trace Circular Buffer"]
    Task["OS Protothread"] -->|SYN_TRACE| RingBuffer
    RingBuffer -->|syn_trace_dump| CLI["Serial CLI / Post-Mortem Log"]

docs.title: Complete Code Example
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/debug/syn_trace.h>

#define EVT_SYSTEM_START    0x0001
#define EVT_SENSOR_READ     0x0002
#define EVT_PACKET_RX       0x0003
#define EVT_ERROR_OVERFLOW  0x00E0

static SYN_TraceEntry trace_buffer[64];
static SYN_Trace trace;

void debug_print(const char *msg) {
    printf("%s", msg);
}

void app_init(void) {
    // Initialize circular buffer with 64 entries
    syn_trace_init(&trace, trace_buffer, 64);

    // Record system startup event
    SYN_TRACE(&trace, EVT_SYSTEM_START, 0);
}

void on_uart_packet_received(uint16_t length) {
    // Record event ID + length payload (millisecond timestamp via syn_port_get_tick_ms())
    SYN_TRACE(&trace, EVT_PACKET_RX, length);
}

void dump_trace_log(void) {
    // Dump formatted event history over serial
    syn_trace_dump(&trace, debug_print);
}

docs.title: 2. Task CPU Profiler (syn_profiler.h)
docs.text: The syn_profiler module measures per-task execution duration, CPU share, peak single-run time, and execution counts when wrapped around task dispatches (syn_profiler_task_begin() / syn_profiler_task_end()). It does not hook into syn_sched automatically; wrap the task bodies or custom dispatch calls you want to instrument. (For microsecond-granularity yield-latency tracking via syn_port_get_tick_us(), see syntropic/debug/syn_task_profile.h.)

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Tracks task execution time via syn_port_get_tick_ms() (reported in µs).
  • Calculates CPU percentage with 0.1% resolution (cpu_percent_x10).
  • Retains high-watermark peak run time (peak_us) across evaluation periods.
  • Outputs formatted diagnostic tables via callback (syn_profiler_dump()).

docs.title: Complete Code Example
docs.text:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <syntropic/debug/syn_profiler.h>

static SYN_ProfileEntry prof_entries[3];
static SYN_Profiler profiler;
static uint32_t last_dump_ms;

void cli_print_line(const char *line) {
    printf("%s", line);
}

void app_setup_profiler(void) {
    // Initialize profiler with 3 caller-owned profile entries
    syn_profiler_init(&profiler, prof_entries, 3);

    syn_profiler_register(&profiler, 0, "SensorTask");
    syn_profiler_register(&profiler, 1, "CommTask");
    syn_profiler_register(&profiler, 2, "DisplayTask");
    last_dump_ms = syn_port_get_tick_ms();
}

void scheduler_loop(void) {
    // 1. Profile Task 0 (SensorTask)
    syn_profiler_task_begin(&profiler, 0);
    run_sensor_task();
    syn_profiler_task_end(&profiler, 0);

    // 2. Profile Task 1 (CommTask)
    syn_profiler_task_begin(&profiler, 1);
    run_comm_task();
    syn_profiler_task_end(&profiler, 1);

    // 3. Periodically update percentages & dump stats (every 1000 ms)
    if ((syn_port_get_tick_ms() - last_dump_ms) >= 1000U) {
        last_dump_ms = syn_port_get_tick_ms();
        syn_profiler_update(&profiler);
        syn_profiler_dump(&profiler, cli_print_line);
    }
}

docs.text:
--- CPU Profiler (Period: 1000 ms) ---
Task            CPU %      Peak (us)   Runs
--------------------------------------------
SensorTask      12.5%        1420 us    100
CommTask         4.2%         320 us     50
DisplayTask     28.1%        4800 us     10

docs.title: 3. Cooperative Yield-Latency & Chunk-Budget Profiler (syn_task_profile.h)
docs.text:
syn_task_profile (SYN_USE_PROFILER) measures microsecond-resolution uninterrupted step durations (max_yield_us) via syn_port_get_tick_us() and integrates directly with SYN_Sched via syn_sched_set_profiler().

  • Zero per-task RAM overhead when unused: sizeof(SYN_Task) is unchanged; SYN_Sched holds a single nullable SYN_TaskProfileManager * pointer when SYN_USE_PROFILER is enabled.
  • Cooperative budget contract check: syn_task_profile_check_budgets(&prof, &sched, &violations, &worst) compares each profiled task's max_yield_us against the tightest max_wait_ms * 1000 among all participating peer tasks in sched (excluding SYN_TASK_SUSPENDED slots and unprofiled SYN_TASK_DEAD slots).
#include <syntropic/syntropic.h>

static SYN_TaskProfileManager g_prof;

void attach_budget_profiler(SYN_Sched *sched)
{
    syn_task_profile_init(&g_prof);
    syn_sched_set_profiler(sched, &g_prof);
}

bool check_cooperative_budgets(const SYN_Sched *sched)
{
    size_t violations = 0U;
    SYN_TaskBudgetViolation worst;
    if (syn_task_profile_check_budgets(&g_prof, sched, &violations, &worst) != SYN_OK) {
        return false;
    }
    return violations == 0U;
}

docs.title: Display & UI Modules
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides hardware-independent framebuffer drawing (syn_canvas), 2D graphics primitives (syn_gfx), and a zero-allocation immediate-mode GUI engine (syn_imgui).

docs.title: 1. Framebuffer Display Canvas (display/syn_canvas.h)
docs.text: The syn_canvas driver (SYN_USE_CANVAS) provides a hardware-agnostic framebuffer supporting both 1bpp (Monochrome OLED) and 16bpp (RGB565 TFT) displays. Companion header display/syn_gfx.h (SYN_GfxContext, selected via SYN_GFX_BACKEND = SYN_GFX_BACKEND_CANVAS) wraps syn_canvas_* primitives (syn_gfx_clear, syn_gfx_line, syn_gfx_rect_fill, syn_gfx_text, syn_gfx_set_clip, syn_gfx_flush) as zero-overhead compile-time macros used by syn_imgui and application rendering code.

docs.title: Architecture Data Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Drawing["Drawing Primitives (line, text, rect)"] --> Canvas["SYN_Canvas Framebuffer"]
    Canvas -->|syn_canvas_flush| HardwareFn["Flush Function (SPI/I2C DMA)"]
    HardwareFn --> OLED["Physical OLED / TFT Display"]

docs.title: Complete Code Example (SSD1306 Mono OLED)
docs.text:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <syntropic/display/syn_canvas.h>

// Monochrome OLED (128×64 pixels, 1bpp = 1024 bytes)
static uint8_t framebuf[128 * 64 / 8];
static SYN_Canvas canvas;

// Flush callback: sends raw framebuffer bytes to display driver over I2C/SPI
static void oled_flush_callback(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    // Send 1024-byte framebuffer via I2C/SPI DMA
    SSD1306_Transmit_Buffer(buf, len);
}

void display_setup(void) {
    // Initialize canvas: 128px width, 64px height, 1bpp monochrome format
    syn_canvas_init(&canvas, framebuf, 128, 64, 1, oled_flush_callback, NULL);
}

void render_dashboard(int temperature, int battery_pct) {
    char str[32];

    // Clear previous frame
    syn_canvas_clear(&canvas);

    // Draw header text using built-in 5x7 font (color 1 = white on 1bpp)
    syn_canvas_text(&canvas, 0, 0, "SyntropicOS Dashboard", 1);

    // Draw horizontal dividing line
    syn_canvas_line(&canvas, 0, 10, 127, 10, 1);

    // Draw metric labels
    snprintf(str, sizeof(str), "Temp: %d C", temperature);
    syn_canvas_text(&canvas, 0, 20, str, 1);

    snprintf(str, sizeof(str), "Batt: %d%%", battery_pct);
    syn_canvas_text(&canvas, 0, 32, str, 1);

    // Draw battery level progress bar outline & fill
    syn_canvas_rect(&canvas, 70, 32, 50, 8, 1); // Outline
    syn_canvas_rect_fill(&canvas, 71, 33, (int16_t)((battery_pct * 48) / 100), 6, 1); // Fill

    // Push framebuffer to hardware
    syn_canvas_flush(&canvas);
}

docs.title: 2. Immediate-Mode GUI (ui/syn_imgui.h)
docs.text: The syn_imgui module provides a zero-allocation Immediate-Mode GUI framework. Widgets are drawn and input-tested in a single pass each frame without maintaining complex DOM trees or allocating dynamic heap memory.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Widgets: Buttons, Sliders, Checkboxes, Progress Bars, Gauges, Real-time Graphs.
  • Navigation: Rotary Encoder step navigation, Button clicks, or Touchscreen X/Y coordinates.

docs.title: Complete IMGUI Menu Example
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/display/syn_canvas.h>
#include <syntropic/ui/syn_imgui.h>

static SYN_IMGUI_Context ui;
static bool heater_enabled = false;
static int32_t target_temp = 25;

void gui_setup(void) {
    syn_imgui_init(&ui);
}

void render_gui(SYN_Canvas *canvas, bool btn_select, bool btn_back, int32_t enc_delta) {
    syn_canvas_clear(canvas);
    syn_imgui_begin(&ui, canvas, btn_select, btn_back, enc_delta, false, 0, 0);

    syn_imgui_label(&ui, "Temperature Control", 10, 5);

    // Interactive Checkbox widget
    if (syn_imgui_checkbox(&ui, "Enable Heater", &heater_enabled, 10, 18, 108, 12)) {
        // Toggle callback logic
    }

    // Interactive Slider widget
    if (heater_enabled) {
        syn_imgui_slider(&ui, "Set Temp", &target_temp, 15, 40, 10, 36, 108, 12);
    }

    syn_imgui_end(&ui);
    syn_canvas_flush(canvas);
}

docs.title: Virtual PIN Keypad (syn_imgui_numpad)
docs.text:
Renders a 4x3 keypad grid (1-9, 0, C Clear, OK Confirm) supporting touch taps and rotary encoder navigation.

static char pin_code[8] = "";

void render_pin_screen(SYN_IMGUI_Context *ctx) {
    // Render 4x3 PIN entry numpad with '*' digit masking
    int status = syn_imgui_numpad(ctx, pin_code, sizeof(pin_code), true, 0, 0, 120, 60);

    if (status == 1) {
        // OK pressed: validate passcode
        if (strcmp(pin_code, "1234") == 0) {
            syn_imgui_toast(ctx, "Access Granted", 2000, current_ms, start_ms);
        } else {
            syn_imgui_toast(ctx, "Invalid PIN", 2000, current_ms, start_ms);
            pin_code[0] = '\0'; // reset
        }
    } else if (status == -1) {
        // Clear/Back pressed on empty buffer: exit screen
        navigate_back();
    }
}

docs.title: Transient Toast Banner (syn_imgui_toast)
docs.text:
Renders a floating notification overlay banner at the top of the display that auto-dismisses after duration_ms.

// Displays a 2-second status notification overlay
syn_imgui_toast(ctx, "Settings Saved!", 2000, current_tick_ms, toast_start_ms);

docs.title: 3. Character LCD & OLED Direct Drivers (display/syn_charlcd.h & display/syn_oled.h)
docs.text:
Supports HD44780 16x2 / 20x4 Character LCD displays (GPIO 4-bit / I2C backpack) and SSD1306 / SH1106 monochrome OLED direct command initialization.

#include <syntropic/display/syn_charlcd.h>

static SYN_CharLCD lcd;

void charlcd_demo(SYN_GPIO_Pin scl_pin, SYN_GPIO_Pin sda_pin) {
    syn_charlcd_init_i2c(&lcd, scl_pin, sda_pin, 0x27, 16, 2);
    syn_charlcd_set_cursor(&lcd, 0, 0);
    syn_charlcd_print(&lcd, "SyntropicOS");
}

docs.title: 4. 7-Segment LED Multiplex Driver (display/syn_seg7.h)
docs.text:
Multiplexed 7-segment digital display driver supporting decimal integers, floating-point rendering, and custom hexadecimal patterns.

#include <syntropic/display/syn_seg7.h>

static SYN_Seg7 seg;

void seg7_demo(const SYN_GPIO_Pin seg_pins[8], const SYN_GPIO_Pin digit_pins[4]) {
    syn_seg7_init(&seg, seg_pins, digit_pins, 4, SYN_SEG7_COMMON_CATHODE);
    // Render float number 12.34 across 4 digits
    syn_seg7_print_float(&seg, 12.34f, 2);
    syn_seg7_scan(&seg); // Call periodically to multiplex digits
}

docs.title: 5. Declarative Hierarchical Menu System (ui/syn_menu.h)
docs.text: SYN_Menu (SYN_USE_MENU) navigates ROM-resident menu trees (SYN_MENU_ROOT, SYN_MENU_SUBMENU, SYN_MENU_CALLBACK, SYN_MENU_TOGGLE, SYN_MENU_VALUE) using a fixed-depth parent stack (SYN_MENU_MAX_DEPTH = 8) and a caller-supplied renderer callback (syn_menu_init, syn_menu_up, syn_menu_down, syn_menu_enter, syn_menu_back, syn_menu_render) suitable for character LCDs, OLEDs, or rotary-encoder front panels.

docs.title: Hardware Peripheral Drivers
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides portable hardware abstraction drivers for GPIO, UART, ADC, DAC, CAN, SPI, I2C, RTC, and DMA. Every driver is guarded by compile-time configuration switches (SYN_USE_*).

docs.title: Technical Specifications
docs.text: Feature Specification Port Interface Hardware-independent wrapper calling syn_port_* interfaces. ISR Safety UART and DMA drivers use lock-free SPSC ring buffers for safe ISR-to-task transfers. Memory Allocation 100% Static / Zero Heap. All driver instances are caller-owned structures.

docs.title: Driver Dataflow Pipeline (UART + DMA Example)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    HW["Hardware Peripheral (UART / ADC)"] -->|ISR / DMA Interrupt| RingBuf["SPSC Ring Buffer (syn_ringbuf)"]
    RingBuf -->|syn_uart_read| Task["Cooperative Protothread Task"]
    Task --> Processing["Process Byte Stream"]

docs.title: 1. GPIO & Digital I/O (drivers/syn_gpio.h)
docs.text:
Provides pin initialization, reading, writing, toggling, and mode configuration (Input, Output, Pull-Up, Pull-Down, Open-Drain).

#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_gpio.h>

void gpio_demo(void) {
    // Initialize pin 13 as Output
    syn_gpio_init(13, SYN_GPIO_OUTPUT);

    // Toggle pin state
    syn_gpio_toggle(13);

    // Read input level
    SYN_GPIO_State state = syn_gpio_read(12);
}

docs.title: 2. Buffered Serial UART (drivers/syn_uart.h)
docs.text:
Buffered UART driver using lock-free SPSC ring buffers for high-speed RX/TX without data loss.

#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_uart.h>

static SYN_UART uart;

void uart_setup(void) {
    // Initialize UART 1 at 115200 8N1 (TX/RX ring buffers embedded in SYN_UART)
    syn_uart_init(&uart, 1, 115200);
}

void USART1_IRQHandler(void) {
    // ISR feed: safe to call from interrupt context
    uint8_t rx_byte = (uint8_t)USART1->DR;
    syn_uart_rx_isr_feed(&uart, rx_byte);

    // ISR flush: drain TX ring buffer asynchronously
    syn_uart_tx_isr_flush(&uart);
}

void uart_send_nonblocking(const uint8_t *data, size_t len) {
    // Non-blocking bulk write into TX ring buffer
    if (syn_uart_write_async(&uart, data, len) == SYN_OK) {
        // Wait until tx_rb is empty AND hardware shift register is clear (RS485 DE safety)
        // syn_uart_tx_complete(&uart)
    }
}

docs.title: 3. Analog-to-Digital Converter (drivers/syn_adc.h)
docs.text:
Provides single-shot 12-bit raw conversion, calibrated millivolt reading (mV), and multi-channel SRAM background scanning via DMA.

#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_adc.h>

static SYN_ADC adc0;

void adc_setup(void) {
    SYN_ADC_Config cfg = {
        .adc_id = 0,
        .channel_mask = (1U << 0),
        .vref_mv = 3300,
        .use_dma = false,
    };
    syn_adc_init(&adc0, &cfg);
}

void read_voltage(void) {
    uint16_t raw = syn_adc_read_raw(&adc0, 0);
    uint32_t millivolts = syn_adc_read_mv(&adc0, 0);
    printf("Channel 0: raw=%u, %lu mV\n", (unsigned int)raw, (unsigned long)millivolts);
}

docs.title: 4. DMA Transaction Engine (drivers/syn_dma.h)
docs.text:
Bare-metal safe DMA transaction engine featuring address alignment verification, D-cache invalidation, and atomic busy protection.

#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_dma.h>

static SYN_DMA dma;

void on_dma_complete(SYN_DMA *dma_inst, SYN_DMA_Event event, void *ctx) {
    (void)dma_inst;
    (void)ctx;
    if ((event & SYN_DMA_EVENT_COMPLETE) != 0) {
        printf("DMA Transfer Complete!\n");
    }
}

void start_dma_transfer(const uint32_t *src, uint32_t *dst, size_t count) {
    SYN_DMA_Config cfg = {
        .channel_id = 0,
        .dir = SYN_DMA_DIR_MEM_TO_MEM,
        .data_size = SYN_DMA_SIZE_32BIT,
        .src_inc = true,
        .dst_inc = true,
        .callback = on_dma_complete,
        .user_ctx = NULL,
    };
    syn_dma_init(&dma, &cfg);
    syn_dma_start(&dma, (const void *)src, (void *)dst, count);
}

docs.title: 7. Shift Register & I/O Expander (drivers/syn_shiftreg.h & drivers/syn_ioexp.h)
docs.text:
Supports 74HC595 output expansion, 74HC165 input reading, and MCP23017 / PCF8574 I2C GPIO expanders.

#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_shiftreg.h>
#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_ioexp.h>

static SYN_ShiftRegOut sr;
static SYN_IOExp ioexp;

void expander_demo(void) {

    syn_shiftreg_out_init(&sr, 2, 3, 4, 1);
    syn_shiftreg_out_write_byte(&sr, 0, 0xAA);
    syn_shiftreg_out_flush(&sr);

}

#include <syntropic/drivers/syn_usb_host.h>

docs.title: DSP & Digital Signal Processing Modules
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides fixed-point (integer-only) Digital Signal Processing (DSP) components designed for microcontrollers without Hardware Floating-Point Units (FPUs).

docs.title: Technical Specifications
docs.text: Feature Specification Math Representation Q16.16 Fixed-Point (q16_t). 16 bits integer, 16 bits fractional. Accumulator Resolution 64-bit integer (int64_t) to prevent overflow during sum/square accumulation. Memory Allocation 100% Static / Zero Heap. Buffers are caller-owned.

docs.title: 1. Digital Filters (dsp/syn_filter.h & dsp/syn_biquad.h)
docs.text: SyntropicOS includes Moving Average, Exponential Moving Average (EMA), Median spike rejection, Direct-Form FIR, and Butterworth Biquad IIR filters.

docs.title: Signal Processing Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    RawADC["Raw ADC Sample"] --> MedianFilter["Median Filter (Spike Removal)"]
    MedianFilter --> EMAFilter["EMA / Biquad Filter (Noise Reduction)"]
    EMAFilter --> SignalStats["Signal Statistics (Min, Max, Mean, RMS)"]

docs.title: Complete Code Example (Biquad Butterworth Lowpass Filter)
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/dsp/syn_biquad.h>
#include <syntropic/dsp/syn_filter.h>

static SYN_FilterBiquad lpf;
static SYN_FilterEMA    ema;

void dsp_init(void) {
    // 1. Initialize EMA Filter (alpha = 64/256 = 0.25)
    syn_filter_ema_init(&ema, 64);

    // 2. Initialize 2nd-order Butterworth Lowpass Filter: 100 Hz cutoff, 1000 Hz sample rate
    syn_filter_biquad_lowpass(&lpf, Q16_FROM_INT(100), Q16_FROM_INT(1000));
}

int16_t process_adc_sample(int16_t raw_sample) {
    // Convert sample to Q16.16 fixed-point format
    q16_t in_q16 = Q16_FROM_INT(raw_sample);

    // Filter through lowpass Biquad
    q16_t filtered_q16 = syn_filter_biquad_update(&lpf, in_q16);

    // Return integer result
    return (int16_t)Q16_TO_INT(filtered_q16);
}

docs.title: 2. Signal Statistics (dsp/syn_signal.h)
docs.text:
Provides real-time sliding window statistics (min, max, mean, variance, standard deviation, RMS) over a caller-owned circular buffer.

#include <syntropic/dsp/syn_signal.h>

static int32_t stats_buffer[64];
static SYN_Signal sig;

void stats_init(void) {
    syn_signal_init(&sig, stats_buffer, 64);
}

void on_adc_sample(int32_t val) {
    syn_signal_push(&sig, val);

    int32_t min_val = syn_signal_min(&sig);
    int32_t max_val = syn_signal_max(&sig);
    int32_t mean_val = syn_signal_mean(&sig);
    int32_t rms_val  = syn_signal_rms_q16(&sig);
}

docs.title: 3. Fast Fourier Transform & Peak Detection (dsp/syn_fft.h)
docs.text:
Provides fixed-point Radix-2 FFT spectral analysis, Hanning/Hamming windowing, peak frequency identification, and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) calculation.

#include <syntropic/dsp/syn_fft.h>

#define FFT_SIZE 64

static q16_t real_buf[FFT_SIZE];
static q16_t imag_buf[FFT_SIZE];
static q16_t win_buf[FFT_SIZE];
static q16_t mag_buf[FFT_SIZE / 2 + 1];

void analyze_spectrum(void) {
    // Generate and apply Hanning window
    syn_fft_window_hanning(win_buf, FFT_SIZE);
    for (uint16_t i = 0; i < FFT_SIZE; i++) {
        real_buf[i] = q16_mul(real_buf[i], win_buf[i]);
    }

    // Perform in-place Radix-2 FFT
    syn_dsp_fft(real_buf, imag_buf, FFT_SIZE);

    // Compute magnitude spectrum (FFT_SIZE / 2 + 1 bins)
    syn_fft_magnitude_spectrum(real_buf, imag_buf, mag_buf, FFT_SIZE);

    // Find dominant frequency peak (at 1000 Hz sample rate)
    SYN_FFTPeak peak;
    uint8_t found = 0;
    syn_fft_find_peaks(mag_buf, FFT_SIZE / 2 + 1, Q16_FROM_INT(1000), &peak, 1, &found);
}

docs.title: 4. TinyML & Fixed-Point Neural Networks (util/syn_nn.h)
docs.text: SyntropicOS features a zero-heap, fixed-point TinyML inference engine tailored for edge sensor processing (e.g., Human Activity Recognition, vibration fault detection, anomaly classification).

docs.title: Key Neural Network Features
docs.text:
• Quantized 1D Convolution (syn_nn_conv1d_quant_q7): Multi-channel temporal feature extraction with TFLite-style affine quantization scaling.
  • Quantized Dense Layers (syn_nn_dense_quant_q7): Fully connected layers supporting arbitrary activation functions.
  • 1D Max & Average Pooling (syn_nn_maxpool1d_q7 / syn_nn_avgpool1d_q7): INT8 temporal downsampling.
  • Self-Attention Transformer Engine (syn_nn_attention_q7): Multi-head / single-head QKV dot-product self-attention mechanism.
  • Stackless Protothread Coroutines (syn_nn_conv1d_pt / syn_nn_dense_pt): Time-sliced inference that yields execution back to the RTOS event loop every chunk_size steps without stack memory overhead.

docs.title: Complete Code Example (Affine-Quantized 1D-CNN Inference)
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/util/syn_nn.h>

// Scaled affine quantization parameters
static const syn_nn_quant_t layer1_quant = {
    .multiplier = 32768, // Fixed-point multiplier (Q15)
    .shift = 1,          // Bit-shift
    .zero_point = 0      // INT8 zero-point offset
};

void run_sensor_inference(const q7_t *sensor_data, q7_t *class_probabilities) {
    q7_t conv_out[16 * 32];
    q7_t pool_out[8 * 32];

    // 1. 1D Convolution: 16 time steps, 3 accelerometer channels -> 32 filters, 3x1 kernel
    syn_nn_conv1d_quant_q7(sensor_data, 16, 3, conv1_weights, conv1_biases,
                           conv_out, 32, 3, 1, SYN_NN_ACT_RELU, &layer1_quant);

    // 2. 1D Max Pooling: Pool size 2, Stride 2 (16 steps -> 8 steps)
    syn_nn_maxpool1d_q7(conv_out, 16, 32, pool_out, 2, 2);

    // 3. Dense Classifier Output
    syn_nn_dense_quant_q7(pool_out, 8 * 32, dense_weights, dense_biases,
                          class_probabilities, 6, SYN_NN_ACT_NONE, &layer1_quant);

    // 4. ArgMax Class Index Selection
    size_t predicted_activity = syn_nn_argmax_q7(class_probabilities, 6);
}

docs.title: 5. Waveform Synthesis, Tone Detection, Kalman Estimation & Audio Features
docs.text:
• Runtime Biquad Filter Designer (dsp/syn_filter_design.h, requires SYN_USE_BIQUAD & SYN_USE_QMATH): Computes normalized Q16.16 second-order IIR coefficients (SYN_BiquadCoeffs) at runtime for lowpass, highpass, bandpass, and notch responses (syn_filter_design_lowpass/highpass/bandpass/notch, syn_filter_design_apply_to_biquad).
  • Direct Digital Synthesis (dsp/syn_dds.h, SYN_USE_DDS): 32-bit phase-accumulator waveform generator (SYN_DDS: syn_dds_init, syn_dds_step, syn_dds_fill_q16, syn_dds_fill_u16) producing sine, triangle, sawtooth, variable-duty square, and white-noise signals for DAC or test injection.
  • Goertzel Single-Bin Tone Detector (dsp/syn_goertzel.h, SYN_USE_GOERTZEL): SYN_Goertzel (syn_goertzel_init, syn_goertzel_process_sample, syn_goertzel_process_block, syn_goertzel_get_magnitude_sq) computes Q15 single-frequency |X(k)|^2 power for DTMF and pilot-tone detection without full FFT cost.
  • Fixed-Point Linear Kalman Filter (dsp/syn_kalman.h, SYN_USE_KALMAN): Discrete-time Q16.16 state estimator (SYN_Kalman: syn_kalman_init, syn_kalman_predict, syn_kalman_update) operating on caller-allocated SYN_Matrix state/covariance workspaces (SYN_KALMAN_SCRATCH_DECL).
  • MFCC & DCT-II Spectral Features (dsp/syn_mfcc.h, SYN_USE_MFCC; dsp/syn_dsp.h): syn_mfcc_process_frame() extracts 13 quantized q7_t Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients across 26 Mel filterbanks from 16-bit PCM frames; syn_dsp_dct2_q7() computes standalone q7_t Type-II Discrete Cosine Transforms.

docs.title: Cross-Module System Integration
docs.text: SyntropicOS modules compose directly with each other. When multiple modules are enabled in syn_config.h, cross-module integrations automatically hook together without requiring verbose glue code.

docs.title: Automatic Integration Matrix
docs.text: Source Module Target Module Automatic Integration Behavior Active Object FSM Combines Table-Driven FSM state machine + SYN_Mailbox event queue + caller-owned SYN_Task runner into an event-driven actor. Button FSM Uses syn_fsm state machine internally for debouncing, long-press hold transitions, and combo tracking. Watchdog Error Log Task execution timeout and deadlock events are automatically recorded into syn_errlog when .errlog is configured. CLI Scheduler Built-in CLI command tasks displays each task's name, priority, and state (READY, SUSPENDED, DEAD, BLOCKED) when syn_cli_set_scheduler() is invoked. CLI Error Log Built-in CLI command errors dumps circular error log history over serial when syn_cli_set_errlog() is invoked. CLI Version Built-in CLI command version automatically reports SyntropicOS kernel version, target architecture, and build timestamps. Param Store CRC-16 Uses syn_crc16_ccitt() for flash payload validation and corruption detection. Modbus CRC-16 Uses syn_crc16_modbus() for RTU frame validation.

docs.title: 1. CLI + Scheduler & Error Log Integration
docs.text:
Attaching the scheduler and error logger to the Serial CLI exposes instant runtime diagnostics over UART without writing custom CLI commands:

#include <syntropic/cli/syn_cli.h>
#include <syntropic/sched/syn_sched.h>

static SYN_CLI cli;
static SYN_Sched sched;

void app_setup_diagnostics(void) {
    // 1. Initialize CLI & Scheduler...

    // 2. Attach scheduler to CLI: automatically enables the 'tasks' command
    syn_cli_set_scheduler(&sched);
}

docs.title: CLI Terminal Output (> tasks)
docs.text:
> tasks
Tasks:
  serial  prio=0  READY
  sensor  prio=1  BLOCKED
  blink  prio=2  READY
  logger  prio=3  SUSPENDED

docs.title: 2. Active Object Pattern (syn_ao + syn_fsm)
docs.text: The Active Object (AO) integration combines three core primitives: 1. FSM State Machine (syn_fsm): Manages state transitions. 2. Event Mailbox (SYN_Mailbox): Buffers incoming SYN_AO_Event items (mailbox_cap >= 2; usable depth is mailbox_cap - 1). 3. Caller-Owned Scheduler Task (SYN_Task): Binds an entry in the application's SYN_Task[] array to the internal syn_ao_pt_run protothread at the specified SYN_Prio, parking in SYN_TASK_BLOCKED when empty and resuming automatically on syn_ao_post().

docs.title: Active Object Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    EventProducer["Async Interrupt / Driver"] -->|syn_ao_post| EventQueue["SYN_Mailbox"]
    EventQueue -->|Protothread Task Run| AOTask["syn_ao_pt_run (internal)"]
    AOTask -->|Dispatch Event| FSM["SYN_FSM State Machine"]
    FSM --> StateAction["Execute State Action Callback"]

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/sched/syn_ao.h>
#include <syntropic/sched/syn_sched.h>

enum { ST_IDLE = 0, ST_ACTIVE };
enum { EV_START = 1, EV_STOP };

static void on_start(void *ctx) {
    SYN_ActiveObject *ao = (SYN_ActiveObject *)ctx;
    (void)ao; // Access dispatched event payload via ao->last_event.data
}

static const SYN_FSM_Transition motor_transitions[] = {
    { ST_IDLE,   EV_START, ST_ACTIVE, NULL, on_start },
    { ST_ACTIVE, EV_STOP,  ST_IDLE,   NULL, NULL     },
    SYN_FSM_END
};

static SYN_Task tasks[2];
static SYN_Sched sched;
static SYN_ActiveObject motor_ao;
static SYN_AO_Event motor_mbox_buf[9]; // mailbox_cap = 9 (8 usable event slots)

void app_ao_setup(void) {
    syn_ao_init(&motor_ao, &tasks[0], "motor_ao", SYN_PRIO_HIGH,
                motor_transitions, ST_IDLE, motor_mbox_buf, 9);
    syn_task_create(&tasks[1], "housekeep", housekeep_task, SYN_PRIO_LOW, NULL);

    syn_sched_init(&sched, tasks, 2);
}

// ISR-safe and task-safe — queues event and wakes tasks[0] automatically:
void exti_start_irq(void) {
    syn_ao_post(&motor_ao, EV_START, NULL);
}

docs.title: Input / Output Modules
docs.text: SyntropicOS provides non-blocking, debounced drivers for physical user inputs (Buttons, Rotary Encoders) and output indicators (LEDs, Software PWM).

docs.title: 1. Button Driver (syn_button.h)
docs.text: The syn_button driver provides debounced GPIO button management with built-in support for: - Debouncing filter with configurable debounce_ms window. - Active-High and Active-Low pin polarities. - Multi-click tap detection (Single, Double, Triple, N-click). - Long-press hold thresholds and auto-repeat streaming. - Multi-button chorded combinations (SYN_ButtonCombo).

docs.title: Basic Initialization & Single Click
docs.text:
#include <syntropic/input/syn_button.h>

static SYN_Button btn1;

void on_single_click(SYN_Button *btn, void *ctx) {
    // Fired after multi-click window (250ms) expires
}

void app_setup(void) {
    // Port A Pin 2, Active-Low (pull-up), 50ms debounce
    syn_button_init(&btn1, SYN_GPIO_PIN(0, 2), SYN_BUTTON_ACTIVE_LOW, 50);
    syn_button_on_single_click(&btn1, on_single_click, NULL);
}

void app_loop(void) {
    syn_button_update(&btn1);
}

docs.title: Multi-Click & Long-Press Configuration
docs.text:
// Configure 200ms multi-click evaluation window
syn_button_set_click_window(&btn1, 200);

// Register tap gesture handlers
syn_button_on_single_click(&btn1, on_single, NULL);
syn_button_on_double_click(&btn1, on_double, NULL);
syn_button_on_triple_click(&btn1, on_triple, NULL);
syn_button_on_multi_click(&btn1, on_multi, NULL); // 4+ taps

// Register long press (fires ONCE at 1000ms hold threshold)
syn_button_on_long_press(&btn1, on_long_press, 1000, NULL);

// Register auto-repeat (fires every 100ms while held)
syn_button_on_repeat(&btn1, on_repeat, 100, NULL);

[!NOTE] Entering a Long Press (on_long_press) or firing Auto-Repeat (on_repeat) automatically resets the click counter (click_count = 0), preventing single-click callbacks from triggering when the button is released.

docs.title: Multi-Button Combinations (SYN_ButtonCombo)
docs.text:
SYN_ButtonCombo enables chorded multi-button presses (e.g. pressing BTN1 + BTN2 simultaneously).

static SYN_Button btn1;
static SYN_Button btn2;
static SYN_ButtonCombo combo;
static const SYN_Button *combo_list[2];

void on_combo_fired(SYN_Button *btn, void *ctx) {
    // Fired when BTN1 and BTN2 are both pressed
}

void app_setup(void) {
    syn_button_init(&btn1, SYN_GPIO_PIN(0, 2), SYN_BUTTON_ACTIVE_LOW, 50);
    syn_button_init(&btn2, SYN_GPIO_PIN(0, 3), SYN_BUTTON_ACTIVE_LOW, 50);

    combo_list[0] = &btn1;
    combo_list[1] = &btn2;
    syn_button_combo_init(&combo, combo_list, 2, on_combo_fired, NULL);
}

void app_loop(void) {
    syn_button_update(&btn1);
    syn_button_update(&btn2);
    syn_button_combo_update(&combo);
}

docs.title: 3. Non-Blocking LED Driver (syn_led.h)

Provides pattern blinking, flash sequences, and Morse-code style pattern strings.

#include <syntropic/output/syn_led.h>

static SYN_LED status_led;

void setup(void) {
    syn_led_init(&status_led, LED_BUILTIN, SYN_LED_ACTIVE_HIGH);

docs.title: 5. Matrix Keypad & Touch (syn_keypad.h & syn_touch.h)

Scanning matrix keypads ($3\times4$, $4\times4$) and capacitive touch sensor inputs with debouncing.

#include <syntropic/input/syn_keypad.h>
#include <syntropic/input/syn_touch.h>

static SYN_Keypad kp;
static const SYN_GPIO_Pin row_pins[4] = {0, 1, 2, 3};
static const SYN_GPIO_Pin col_pins[4] = {4, 5, 6, 7};

void keypad_setup(void) {
    syn_keypad_init(&kp, row_pins, 4, col_pins, 4, "123A456B789C*0#D");
}

void keypad_demo(void) {

docs.title: 7. Piezo Buzzer & WS2812 Smart LED (syn_buzzer.h & syn_smartled.h)

Non-blocking piezo buzzer melody/beep generator and WS2812 (NeoPixel) RGB LED bit-bang driver.

#include <syntropic/output/syn_buzzer.h>
#include <syntropic/output/syn_smartled.h>

static SYN_Buzzer buz;
static SYN_SmartLED strip;
static SYN_SmartLEDColor pixels[8];

void audio_visual_demo(void) {
    syn_buzzer_init(&buz, 8, true);
    syn_smartled_init(&strip, 9, 8, pixels, SYN_SMARTLED_ORDER_GRB);

    // Play 1 kHz beep for 100 ms
    syn_buzzer_beep(&buz, 1000, 100);
