            ctx->pc += 4U;
#if defined(SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED) && SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED
            float fval;
            memcpy(&fval, &val, sizeof(float));
            q16_t qval = q16_from_float(fval);
            push_stack(ctx, (uint32_t)qval);
#else
            push_stack64(ctx, (uint64_t)val);
#endif
            break;
        }

        case OP_F64_CONST: {
            if ((uint64_t)ctx->pc + 8ULL > (uint64_t)code_end) {
                ctx->status = SYN_WASM_TRAP_INVALID_MODULE;
                break;
            }
            uint64_t val = 0ULL;
            for (uint32_t i = 0U; i < 8U; i++) {
                val |= ((uint64_t)mod->bytes[ctx->pc + i]) << (i * 8U);
            }
            ctx->pc += 8U;
            push_stack64(ctx, val);
            break;
        }

        /* LCOV_EXCL_START: Wasm floating-point & bulk memory opcode interpreter fallbacks */
        case OP_F32_LOAD:
        case OP_F64_LOAD: {
            uint32_t offset = 0U;
            uint32_t base_addr = 0U;
            if (!wasm_read_memarg(ctx, code_end, &offset) || !pop_stack(ctx, &base_addr)) {
                break;
            }
            uint32_t req = (opcode == OP_F32_LOAD) ? 4U : 8U;
            uint64_t addr = 0ULL;
            if (!wasm_check_mem(ctx, base_addr, offset, req, &addr)) {
                break;
            }
            uint64_t val = 0ULL;
            for (uint32_t i = 0U; i < req; i++) {
                val |= ((uint64_t)ctx->linear_mem[addr + i]) << (i * 8U);
            }
            push_stack64(ctx, val);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_STORE:
        case OP_F64_STORE: {
            uint32_t offset = 0U;
            uint64_t val = 0ULL;
            uint32_t base_addr = 0U;
            if (!wasm_read_memarg(ctx, code_end, &offset) || !pop_stack64(ctx, &val) ||
                !pop_stack(ctx, &base_addr)) {
                break;
            }
            uint32_t req = (opcode == OP_F32_STORE) ? 4U : 8U;
            uint64_t addr = 0ULL;
            if (!wasm_check_mem(ctx, base_addr, offset, req, &addr)) {
                break;
            }
            for (uint32_t i = 0U; i < req; i++) {
                ctx->linear_mem[addr + i] = (uint8_t)((val >> (i * 8U)) & 0xFFU);
            }
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_ADD:
        case OP_F32_SUB:
        case OP_F32_MUL:
        case OP_F32_DIV:
        case OP_F32_ABS:
        case OP_F32_NEG:
        case OP_F32_CEIL:
        case OP_F32_FLOOR:
        case OP_F32_TRUNC:
        case OP_F32_NEAREST:
        case OP_F32_SQRT:
        case OP_F32_MIN:
        case OP_F32_MAX:
        case OP_F32_COPYSIGN: {
#if defined(SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED) && SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED
            wasm_exec_f32_fixed(ctx, opcode);
#else
            /* Standard Native F32 Floating-Point Mode */
            if (opcode == OP_F32_ABS || opcode == OP_F32_NEG || opcode == OP_F32_CEIL ||
                opcode == OP_F32_FLOOR || opcode == OP_F32_TRUNC || opcode == OP_F32_NEAREST ||
                opcode == OP_F32_SQRT) {
                float fa = 0.0f;
                if (!pop_f32(ctx, &fa))
                    break;
                float fres = 0.0f;
                if (opcode == OP_F32_ABS)
                    fres = fabsf(fa);
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_NEG)
                    fres = -fa;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_CEIL)
                    fres = ceilf(fa);
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_FLOOR)
                    fres = floorf(fa);
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_TRUNC)
                    fres = truncf(fa);
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_NEAREST)
                    fres = roundf(fa);
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_SQRT)
                    fres = sqrtf(fa);
                push_f32(ctx, fres);
            } else {
                float fb = 0.0f, fa = 0.0f;
                if (!pop_f32(ctx, &fb) || !pop_f32(ctx, &fa))
                    break;
                float fres = 0.0f;
                if (opcode == OP_F32_ADD)
                    fres = fa + fb;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_SUB)
                    fres = fa - fb;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_MUL)
                    fres = fa * fb;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_DIV)
                    fres = fa / fb;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_MIN)
                    fres = (fa < fb) ? fa : fb;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_MAX)
                    fres = (fa > fb) ? fa : fb;
                else if (opcode == OP_F32_COPYSIGN)
                    fres = copysignf(fa, fb);
                push_f32(ctx, fres);
            }
#endif
            break;
        }

#if !defined(SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED) || !SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED
        case OP_F64_ADD:
        case OP_F64_SUB:
        case OP_F64_MUL:
        case OP_F64_DIV:
        case OP_F64_ABS:
        case OP_F64_NEG:
        case OP_F64_CEIL:
        case OP_F64_FLOOR:
        case OP_F64_TRUNC:
        case OP_F64_NEAREST:
        case OP_F64_SQRT:
        case OP_F64_MIN:
        case OP_F64_MAX:
        case OP_F64_COPYSIGN: {
            if (opcode == OP_F64_ABS || opcode == OP_F64_NEG || opcode == OP_F64_CEIL ||
                opcode == OP_F64_FLOOR || opcode == OP_F64_TRUNC || opcode == OP_F64_NEAREST ||
                opcode == OP_F64_SQRT) {
                double da = 0.0;
                if (!pop_f64(ctx, &da))
                    break;
                double dres = 0.0;
                if (opcode == OP_F64_ABS)
                    dres = fabs(da);
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_NEG)
                    dres = -da;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_CEIL)
                    dres = ceil(da);
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_FLOOR)
                    dres = floor(da);
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_TRUNC)
                    dres = trunc(da);
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_NEAREST)
                    dres = round(da);
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_SQRT)
                    dres = sqrt(da);
                push_f64(ctx, dres);
            } else {
                double db = 0.0, da = 0.0;
                if (!pop_f64(ctx, &db) || !pop_f64(ctx, &da))
                    break;
                double dres = 0.0;
                if (opcode == OP_F64_ADD)
                    dres = da + db;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_SUB)
                    dres = da - db;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_MUL)
                    dres = da * db;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_DIV)
                    dres = da / db;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_MIN)
                    dres = (da < db) ? da : db;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_MAX)
                    dres = (da > db) ? da : db;
                else if (opcode == OP_F64_COPYSIGN)
                    dres = copysign(da, db);
                push_f64(ctx, dres);
            }
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_EQ:
        case OP_F32_NE:
        case OP_F32_LT:
        case OP_F32_GT:
        case OP_F32_LE:
        case OP_F32_GE: {
            float fb = 0.0f, fa = 0.0f;
            if (!pop_f32(ctx, &fb) || !pop_f32(ctx, &fa))
                break;
            bool res = false;
            if (opcode == OP_F32_EQ)
                res = (fa == fb);
            else if (opcode == OP_F32_NE)
                res = (fa != fb);
            else if (opcode == OP_F32_LT)
                res = (fa < fb);
            else if (opcode == OP_F32_GT)
                res = (fa > fb);
            else if (opcode == OP_F32_LE)
                res = (fa <= fb);
            else if (opcode == OP_F32_GE)
                res = (fa >= fb);
            push_stack(ctx, res ? 1 : 0);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F64_EQ:
        case OP_F64_NE:
        case OP_F64_LT:
        case OP_F64_GT:
        case OP_F64_LE:
        case OP_F64_GE: {
            double db = 0.0, da = 0.0;
            if (!pop_f64(ctx, &db) || !pop_f64(ctx, &da))
                break;
            bool res = false;
            if (opcode == OP_F64_EQ)
                res = (da == db);
            else if (opcode == OP_F64_NE)
                res = (da != db);
            else if (opcode == OP_F64_LT)
                res = (da < db);
            else if (opcode == OP_F64_GT)
                res = (da > db);
            else if (opcode == OP_F64_LE)
                res = (da <= db);
            else if (opcode == OP_F64_GE)
                res = (da >= db);
            push_stack(ctx, res ? 1 : 0);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_CONVERT_I32_S:
        case OP_F32_CONVERT_I32_U: {
            uint32_t ia = 0;
            if (!pop_stack(ctx, &ia))
                break;
            float fres = (opcode == OP_F32_CONVERT_I32_S) ? (float)(int32_t)ia : (float)ia;
            push_f32(ctx, fres);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_CONVERT_I64_S:
        case OP_F32_CONVERT_I64_U: {
            uint64_t ia = 0;
            if (!pop_stack64(ctx, &ia))
                break;
            float fres = (opcode == OP_F32_CONVERT_I64_S) ? (float)(int64_t)ia : (float)ia;
            push_f32(ctx, fres);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_DEMOTE_F64: {
            double da = 0.0;
            if (pop_f64(ctx, &da))
                push_f32(ctx, (float)da);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F64_CONVERT_I32_S:
        case OP_F64_CONVERT_I32_U: {
            uint32_t ia = 0;
            if (!pop_stack(ctx, &ia))
                break;
            double dres = (opcode == OP_F64_CONVERT_I32_S) ? (double)(int32_t)ia : (double)ia;
            push_f64(ctx, dres);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F64_CONVERT_I64_S:
        case OP_F64_CONVERT_I64_U: {
            uint64_t ia = 0;
            if (!pop_stack64(ctx, &ia))
                break;
            double dres = (opcode == OP_F64_CONVERT_I64_S) ? (double)(int64_t)ia : (double)ia;
            push_f64(ctx, dres);
            break;
        }

        case OP_F64_PROMOTE_F32: {
            float fa = 0.0f;
            if (pop_f32(ctx, &fa))
                push_f64(ctx, (double)fa);
            break;
        }

        case OP_I32_REINTERPRET_F32: {
            float fa = 0.0f;
            if (pop_f32(ctx, &fa)) {
                uint32_t u32;
                memcpy(&u32, &fa, sizeof(u32));
                push_stack(ctx, u32);
            }
            break;
        }

        case OP_I64_REINTERPRET_F64: {
            double da = 0.0;
            if (pop_f64(ctx, &da)) {
                uint64_t u64;
                memcpy(&u64, &da, sizeof(u64));
                push_stack64(ctx, u64);
            }
            break;
        }

        case OP_F32_REINTERPRET_I32: {
            uint32_t u32 = 0;
            if (pop_stack(ctx, &u32)) {
                float fa;
                memcpy(&fa, &u32, sizeof(u32));
                push_f32(ctx, fa);
            }
            break;
        }

        case OP_F64_REINTERPRET_I64: {
            uint64_t u64 = 0;
            if (pop_stack64(ctx, &u64)) {
                double da;
                memcpy(&da, &u64, sizeof(da));
                push_f64(ctx, da);
            }
            break;
        }
#endif
        /* LCOV_EXCL_STOP */

#if !defined(SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED) || !SYN_WASM_USE_FIXED
        case OP_I32_TRUNC_F32_S:
        case OP_I32_TRUNC_F32_U:
        case OP_I32_TRUNC_F64_S:
        case OP_I32_TRUNC_F64_U:
        case OP_I64_TRUNC_F32_S:
        case OP_I64_TRUNC_F32_U:
        case OP_I64_TRUNC_F64_S:
        case OP_I64_TRUNC_F64_U:
            wasm_exec_trunc(ctx, opcode);
            break;
#endif

        case OP_PREFIX_MISC:
            wasm_exec_misc(ctx, code_end);
            break;

        /* LCOV_EXCL_START: Default bad opcode trap */
        default:
            ctx->status = SYN_WASM_TRAP_BAD_OPCODE;
            break;
            /* LCOV_EXCL_STOP */
        }
    }

    if (executed >= max_instructions && ctx->status == SYN_WASM_OK) {
        return SYN_WASM_YIELDED;
    }

    return ctx->status;
}

SYN_PT_Status syn_wasm_exec_pt(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, uint16_t quantum_instructions)
{
    if (pt == NULL || ctx == NULL || ctx->module == NULL) {
        return PT_EXITED;
    }

    uint16_t step_limit =
        (quantum_instructions == 0U) ? SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM : quantum_instructions;

    PT_BEGIN(pt);

    while (ctx->status == SYN_WASM_OK && ctx->call_depth > 0U) {
        SYN_WASM_Status st = syn_wasm_step(ctx, step_limit);
        if (st == SYN_WASM_YIELDED) {
            PT_CONTINUE(pt);
        }
    }

    if (ctx->status != SYN_WASM_HALTED) {
        PT_EXIT(pt);
    }

    PT_END(pt);
}

SYN_PT_Status syn_wasm_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task)
{
    if (pt == NULL || task == NULL || task->user_data == NULL) {
        return PT_EXITED;
    }

    SYN_WASM_Context *ctx = (SYN_WASM_Context *)task->user_data;

    PT_BEGIN(pt);

    while (ctx->status <= SYN_WASM_HALTED) {
        if (ctx->status == SYN_WASM_OK && ctx->call_depth > 0U) {
            if (syn_wasm_step(ctx, SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM) == SYN_WASM_YIELDED) {
                PT_CONTINUE_IF_NEEDED(pt, task);
            }
        } else {
            PT_PASS(pt);
        }
    }

    PT_END(pt);
}

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Warning:

EXPERIMENTAL MODULE - API and bytecode execution semantics subject to change.

Implements a 100% zero-malloc, non-blocking 32-bit WebAssembly MVP interpreter designed for embedded microcontrollers. Supports static linear memory arrays, zero-copy parsing from flash, host function registration, and instruction-sliced cooperative execution with protothread (syn_pt) integration.

Recommended C-to-WASM compilation command for user applications: clang target=wasm32-unknown-unknown -O2 -nostdlib \ -mbulk-memory -msign-ext -mmultivalue -mnontrapping-fptoint \ -Wl,no-entry -Wl,export-all -Wl,allow-undefined \ -Wl,-z,stack-size=1024 app.c -o app.wasm

Child protothread that executes a Wasm function call in instruction quanta. 

SYN_PT_Status syn_wasm_exec_pt (
    SYN_PT * pt,
    SYN_WASM_Context * ctx,
    uint16_t quantum_instructions
)

Steps ctx by quantum_instructions opcodes per slice (defaults to SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM when 0) and yields PT_MORE via PT_CONTINUE(pt) whenever the slice expires with SYN_WASM_YIELDED. Composes directly with PT_SPAWN and PT_SPAWN_IF_NEEDED(pt, task, child, syn_wasm_exec_pt(...)).

Parameters:

  • pt Child protothread control block.
  • ctx Initialized Wasm context with an active syn_wasm_call() frame.
  • quantum_instructions Opcodes per slice (0 uses SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM).

Returns:

PT_MORE while executing, PT_ENDED on SYN_WASM_HALTED, or PT_EXITED on NULL/trap.

docs.title: function syn_wasm_task
docs.text:
Cooperative scheduler task entry point for a WebAssembly VM context. 

SYN_PT_Status syn_wasm_task (
    SYN_PT * pt,
    SYN_Task * task
)

Expects task->user_data to point to an initialized SYN_WASM_Context. Executes active calls in SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM slices and defers via PT_CONTINUE_IF_NEEDED(pt, task) when a peer task requires CPU time, yields PT_IDLE via PT_PASS(pt) when halted or waiting for a new call, and terminates with PT_ENDED if the VM enters a fault trap state.

Parameters:

  • pt Protothread state.
  • task Scheduler task (task->user_data is SYN_WASM_Context *).

Returns:

Protothread status.

#ifndef SYN_WASM_H
#define SYN_WASM_H

#include "../common/syn_defs.h"
#include "../pt/syn_pt.h"
#include "../sched/syn_sched.h"
#include "../util/syn_qmath.h"

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_STACK
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_STACK 64 
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_LOCALS
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_LOCALS 256 
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_CALL_DEPTH
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_CALL_DEPTH 32 
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_FUNCTIONS
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_FUNCTIONS 32 
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_HOST_FUNCS
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_HOST_FUNCS 16 
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_GLOBALS
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_GLOBALS 16 
#endif

#ifndef SYN_WASM_MAX_LABELS
#define SYN_WASM_MAX_LABELS 16 
#endif
#ifndef SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM
#define SYN_WASM_DEFAULT_QUANTUM 64U 
#endif

/* ── Status Codes & Traps ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */

typedef enum {
    SYN_WASM_OK = 0,                   
    SYN_WASM_YIELDED,                  
    SYN_WASM_HALTED,                   
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_STACK_OVERFLOW,      
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_STACK_UNDERFLOW,     
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_OUT_OF_BOUNDS,       
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_BAD_OPCODE,          
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_DIV_ZERO,            
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_UNREACHABLE,         
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_CALL_STACK_OVERFLOW, 
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_TYPE_MISMATCH,       
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_INVALID_MODULE,      
    SYN_WASM_TRAP_UNREGISTERED_HOST    
} SYN_WASM_Status;

/* Forward declarations */
typedef struct SYN_WASM_Context_s SYN_WASM_Context;

typedef uint64_t (*SYN_WASM_HostFunc)(SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, const uint64_t *args, uint8_t argc);

typedef struct {
    uint32_t type_idx;    
    uint32_t code_offset; 
    uint32_t code_size;   
    uint8_t param_count;  
    uint8_t result_count; 
} SYN_WASM_FuncDef;

typedef struct {
    const uint8_t *bytes; 
    uint32_t size;        

    SYN_WASM_FuncDef funcs[SYN_WASM_MAX_FUNCTIONS]; 
    uint16_t func_count;                            
    uint16_t import_func_count;                     

    struct {
        uint32_t name_offset;          
        uint16_t name_len;             
        uint16_t func_idx;             
    } exports[SYN_WASM_MAX_FUNCTIONS]; 
    uint16_t export_count;             

    uint16_t table_elements[64];  
    uint16_t table_element_count; 

    uint32_t start_func_idx; 
    bool has_start_func;     
} SYN_WASM_Module;

/* ── Runtime Call Frame & Label Stacks ───────────────────────────────────── */

typedef struct {
    uint16_t func_idx;   
    uint32_t return_pc;  
    uint32_t frame_sp;   
    uint16_t local_base; 
    uint8_t label_base;  
} SYN_WASM_CallFrame;

typedef struct {
    uint8_t opcode;     
    uint8_t arity;      
    uint32_t target_pc; 
    uint32_t stack_sp;  
} SYN_WASM_Label;

/* ── Runtime Execution Context ────────────────────────────────────────────── */

struct SYN_WASM_Context_s {
    const SYN_WASM_Module *module; 

    uint32_t pc;                        
    uint32_t sp;                        
    uint64_t stack[SYN_WASM_MAX_STACK]; 

    uint64_t locals[SYN_WASM_MAX_LOCALS]; 
    uint16_t local_count;                 

    SYN_WASM_CallFrame call_stack[SYN_WASM_MAX_CALL_DEPTH]; 
    uint8_t call_depth;                                     

    SYN_WASM_Label label_stack[SYN_WASM_MAX_LABELS]; 
    uint8_t label_depth;                             

    uint64_t globals[SYN_WASM_MAX_GLOBALS]; 
    uint16_t global_count;                  

    uint8_t *linear_mem;      
    uint32_t linear_mem_size; 

    SYN_WASM_HostFunc host_funcs[SYN_WASM_MAX_HOST_FUNCS]; 
    uint16_t host_func_count;                              

    void *user_ctx;         
    SYN_WASM_Status status; 
};

/* ── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

bool syn_wasm_module_load(SYN_WASM_Module *mod, const uint8_t *bytes, uint32_t size);

bool syn_wasm_init(SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, const SYN_WASM_Module *mod, uint8_t *linear_mem,
                   uint32_t mem_size);

bool syn_wasm_register_host(SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, uint16_t import_index, SYN_WASM_HostFunc func);

int32_t syn_wasm_find_export(const SYN_WASM_Module *mod, const char *name);

bool syn_wasm_call(SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, uint16_t func_index);

SYN_WASM_Status syn_wasm_step(SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, uint16_t max_instructions);

uint64_t syn_wasm_result(const SYN_WASM_Context *ctx);

SYN_PT_Status syn_wasm_exec_pt(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_WASM_Context *ctx, uint16_t quantum_instructions);

SYN_PT_Status syn_wasm_task(SYN_PT *pt, SYN_Task *task);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* SYN_WASM_H */

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
HOW TO USE: * Copy this file to your project's include path. * Rename the copy to "syn_config.h". * Edit the copy to enable/disable modules and set buffer sizes.

SyntropicOS headers look for "syn_config.h" on the include path. If the file is not found, sensible defaults are used.

docs.title: Class Hierarchy
docs.text:
This inheritance list is sorted roughly, but not completely, alphabetically:

  • struct AES_state2 Bitsliced AES state matrix (8 slices of 32-bit words).
  • struct DirEntryLoc Result of a directory scan — location of a matching or free entry.
  • struct EXTI_Entry EXTI callback table entry.
  • struct FAT_Volume Internal FAT volume metadata parsed from the boot sector.
  • struct OPCUA_Reader Binary deserializer context for OPC UA messages.
  • struct OPCUA_WriteItem Decoded single WriteValue entry from a WriteRequest.
  • struct OPCUA_Writer Binary serializer context for OPC UA messages.
  • struct PhaseGatePattern 3-phase gate driving state pattern per commutation step.
  • struct Poly1305_Ctx Poly1305 context.
  • struct SYN_ADC ADC driver handle structure.
  • struct SYN_ADC_Config ADC driver configuration structure.
  • struct SYN_ADPCM_State IMA-ADPCM Encoder and Decoder State.
  • struct SYN_AES_Context AES context containing expanded round keys.
  • struct SYN_AES_GCM_Context AES-GCM AEAD context — wraps AES key schedule and GHASH subkey/tables.
  • struct SYN_AO_Event Active Object Event.
  • struct SYN_ASN1_Element Parsed ASN.1 TLV element header.
  • struct SYN_AUTOIP
  • struct SYN_ActiveObject Active Object structure.
  • struct SYN_Actuator Linear actuator instance — motor controller + stroke mapping.
  • struct SYN_Actuator_Config Actuator configuration.
  • struct SYN_AtParser AT Command Parser context.
  • struct SYN_Audio Audio Playback Engine Instance State.
  • struct SYN_Audio_Config Audio Playback Configuration.
  • struct SYN_Audio_Mixer Audio Mixer Instance State.
  • struct SYN_Audio_Mixer_Channel State for a single mixer input channel.
  • struct SYN_AutoTune Auto-tuner instance.
  • struct SYN_AutoTune_Config Auto-tuner configuration.
  • struct SYN_AutoTune_Limits Physical constraints for the one-call auto-tune.
  • struct SYN_AutoTune_LogFrame Telemetry frame for Auto-Tune capture.
  • struct SYN_AutoTune_Result Auto-tune results (valid when state == DONE).
  • struct SYN_BACnet_MSTP_Frame Decoded BACnet MS/TP Frame Structure.
  • struct SYN_BACnet_Node BACnet MS/TP Node Context.
  • struct SYN_BACnet_Object BACnet Object Instance Definition.
  • struct SYN_BLAKE2s BLAKE2s hash context — caller-owned.
  • struct SYN_BLDC_6Step
  • struct SYN_BLDC_Config
  • struct SYN_BLDC_PhaseOutputs
  • struct SYN_BLE_GAP_AdvParams
  • struct SYN_BLE_GAP_AdvReport
  • struct SYN_BLE_GAP_ConnInfo
  • struct SYN_BLE_GAP_s
  • struct SYN_BLE_GATT_Attr
  • struct SYN_BLE_GATT_s
  • struct SYN_BLE_HCI_Config
  • struct SYN_BLE_HCI_s
  • struct SYN_BLE_L2CAP_Connection
  • struct SYN_BLE_L2CAP_s
  • struct SYN_Backoff Exponential backoff state.
  • struct SYN_Biometric Generic Biometric Sensor Context.
  • struct SYN_BiquadCoeffs Normalized Biquad filter coefficients (where a0 = 1.0).
  • struct SYN_Blackbox
  • struct SYN_Blackbox_Record
  • struct SYN_Boot Boot manager — crash-loop detection and safe-mode state.
  • struct SYN_BootData Boot data persisted to flash across resets.
  • struct SYN_Button Button descriptor — owns the FSM, debounce, multi-click, and callback state.
  • struct SYN_ButtonCombo Combination button descriptor for simultaneous multi-button presses.
  • struct SYN_Buzzer Non-blocking piezo buzzer context.
  • struct SYN_CAN CAN bus instance — port, bitrate, callbacks, stats.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenManager CANopen Manager Master State Handle.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenNode CANopen Node State Handle.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenNodeConfig CANopen Node Configuration.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenNodeMonitor Remote Node Heartbeat Monitor Entry.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenODEntry Object Dictionary Entry Definition.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenPDOMap PDO Mapping Configuration.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenSDOClient SDO Client Transaction Handle.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenSDOSession Active SDO transfer session tracking.
  • struct SYN_CANOpenTxSlot Queued outbound CANopen frame slot.
  • struct SYN_CAN_Frame CAN bus frame — standard/extended ID, classic CAN or CAN FD.
  • struct SYN_CCP_DAQList DAQ List structure.
  • struct SYN_CCP_MemRegion Registered memory region descriptor for bounds-checked MTA/DAQ access.
  • struct SYN_CCP_ODT ODT (Object Descriptor Table) structure.
  • struct SYN_CCP_ODTEntry ODT Element mapping entry.
  • struct SYN_CCP_Slave CCP Slave Instance Handle.
  • struct SYN_CDR_Reader CDR deserialization input buffer context.
  • struct SYN_CDR_Writer CDR serialization output buffer context.
  • struct SYN_CIA402_Axis CiA 402 Axis Instance.
  • struct SYN_CIA402_Config CiA 402 axis configuration parameters.
  • struct SYN_CIA402_Setpoints CiA 402 motion controller setpoint outputs for motor loop / FOC.
  • struct SYN_CIP_Assembly CIP Assembly Object (Class 0x04) Context.
  • struct SYN_CIP_DeviceNet CIP DeviceNet Object (Class 0x03) Attributes.
  • struct SYN_CIP_Identity CIP Identity Object (Class 0x01) Attributes.
  • struct SYN_CJT188_Decoder Streaming Decoder State Machine for CJ/T 188.
  • struct SYN_CJT188_Frame Decoded CJ/T 188 Protocol Frame.
  • struct SYN_CJT188_MeterData Parsed CJ/T 188 Meter Response Data.
  • struct SYN_CLI CLI instance — command table, line buffer, I/O, and history.
  • struct SYN_CLI_Command Command descriptor.
  • struct SYN_COBS_Decoder Streaming COBS frame decoder.
  • struct SYN_COMP Analog Comparator handle. Caller allocates; zero heap.
  • struct SYN_CRSF_ChannelsFrame
  • struct SYN_CRSF_LinkStats
  • struct SYN_CRSF_Parser
  • struct SYN_CanNM_Config AUTOSAR CAN Network Management Configuration.
  • struct SYN_CanNM_Session AUTOSAR CAN Network Management Session Context.
  • struct SYN_Canvas Canvas instance — framebuffer + drawing state.
  • struct SYN_CborReader CBOR decoder state. Caller-allocated; zero heap.
  • struct SYN_CborWriter CBOR encoder state. Caller-allocated; zero heap.
  • struct SYN_ChangeFilter Dead-band + rate-limited change filter.
  • struct SYN_CharLCD Generic Character LCD Context.
  • struct SYN_CiA303_Indicator CiA 303-3 Status Indicator Handle.
  • struct SYN_CiA401_Device CiA 401 Generic I/O Device State Instance.
  • struct SYN_Climate Generic Climate Sensor Context.
  • struct SYN_CoapBlock CoAP Blockwise Transfer Parameter (RFC 7959).
  • struct SYN_CoapMsg Parsed or to-be-serialized CoAP message header.
  • struct SYN_CoapOption Single CoAP option (number + opaque value).
  • struct SYN_CoapRequest CoAP client request context.
  • struct SYN_CoapTransportRequest CoAP request context over generic SYN_Transport (e.g. DTLS 1.3 / UDP / Serial).
  • struct SYN_ControlReport Human-readable performance report.
  • struct SYN_ControlStats Raw accumulators for control performance analysis.
  • struct SYN_CoreDump Persistent core dump — written to flash on fault.
  • struct SYN_DAC DAC channel handle. Caller allocates; zero heap.
  • struct SYN_DALI_BackwardFrame DALI Backward Frame (Control Gear -> Master, 8-bit payload).
  • struct SYN_DALI_ForwardFrame DALI Forward Frame (Master -> Control Gear, 16-bit payload).
  • struct SYN_DALI_SlaveConfig DALI Slave Configuration.
  • struct SYN_DALI_SlaveState DALI Slave Runtime State.
  • struct SYN_DCMotor DC motor instance — pins, speed, ramp state.
  • struct SYN_DDS DDS Generator State Instance.

  • AUTOSAR CAN NM Control Bit Vector (CBV) Flags

  • CiA 418 Object Dictionary Indices

  • CoAP Message Types

  • CoAP Option Numbers

  • CoAP Request Codes

  • CoAP Response Codes

  • Core & Utilities Core types, status codes, and utility helpers.

  • Cryptography SHA256, ChaCha20Poly1305, Curve25519, and Blake2s primitives.

  • Debug & Diagnostics Logging, profiler, runtime tracing, and CLI commands.

  • Display & UI Canvas graphics primitives and immediate-mode GUI components.

  • Drivers Hardware peripheral driver interfaces (GPIO, UART, I2C, SPI, EXTI, CAN, RTC).

  • DSP & Filters Signal filters, FFT, and data structures.

  • File Opening Flags

  • GB/T 27930 Parameter Group Numbers

  • GB/T 27930 Source Addresses

  • Input / Output LED, button, and encoder interfaces.

  • Input Devices Keypads, buttons, joysticks, touch sensors, and switches.

  • J1939 Reserved Source/Destination Addresses

  • J1939 TP.CM Control Bytes

  • Motor & Control DC motor, servo, stepper, actuator, and PID control algorithms.

  • Networking Packet router, transports, DNS, HTTP, WebSocket, CoAP, and MQTT protocols.

  • Output Devices Buzzers, LEDs, addressable smart LED strips, and actuators.

  • Protocols COBS framing, Modbus, CBOR, and JSON serialization.

  • Scheduling Protothreads, task management, cooperative scheduler, timers, and mailboxes.

  • Seek Origins

  • Sensors Environmental, power, distance, load cell, biometric, and light sensors.

  • Standard J1939 Parameter Group Numbers

  • Standard NMEA 2000 Parameter Group Numbers

  • Storage Virtual Filesystem (VFS) abstraction, settings, and logging.

  • System Bootloader integration, power management, watchdog, faults, and system templates.

  • Utilities String, math, metrics, and helper utilities.

  • VFS Static Limits
